docs.title: C# ENUM Access
docs.text:
Enums live in the mt5_term_api namespace and are used directly as C# enum values:

using mt5_term_api;

// Enum as a method argument
double balance = await account.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance);
var    tick    = await account.SymbolInfoDoubleAsync("EURUSD", SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.SymbolBid);

// Enum inside a request object
var margin = await account.OrderCalcMarginAsync(new OrderCalcMarginRequest
{
    Symbol    = "EURUSD",
    OrderType = ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF.OrderTypeTfBuy,
    Volume    = 0.10,
    OpenPrice = tick.Ask
});

Proto vs C# names. The generated C# member is PascalCase (AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance); its proto OriginalName (as seen on the wire / in .proto files) is ACCOUNT_BALANCE. This table lists the C# member names you write in code.

docs.title: Special Cases
docs.text:
1. AccountInfoInteger and SymbolInfoInteger:

  • Some properties return values that represent an enum but come back as long / int64.
  • These are not typed enums in the reply — just numbers you interpret.

2. ReturnedCode:

  • The ReturnedCode field in trading replies is not an enum.
  • It is a plain uint trade return code (10009 = done; see Return Codes).

3. PriceHistory timeframe:

  • PriceHistoryRequest.Timeframe is an int carrying the MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES value (e.g. PERIOD_H1 = 16385), not a generated C# enum. MT5Sugar.PriceBarsLast accepts a friendly string ("H1") instead.

docs.title: Getting Started with CSharpMT5
docs.text: Quick Setup & Overview - Start automating your trading with CSharpMT5 (C# for MetaTrader 5) in minutes.

docs.title: 🎯 What is CSharpMT5?
docs.text: CSharpMT5 is an industrial-grade, type-safe C# client library for interacting with MetaTrader 5 terminals via high-performance gRPC. It eliminates complex C++ DLL wrappers and provides direct, reliable programmatic trading.

docs.title: 🌟 Key Advantages
docs.text:
• High Throughput: Native gRPC streaming for sub-millisecond price ticks and trade execution.
  • Three-Layer Architecture: Low-level gRPC (MT5Account), typed wrapper methods (MT5Service), and high-level convenience (MT5Sugar).
  • Resilient Connection: Auto-reconnect, exponential backoff, and transparent channel healing.
  • Production Ready: Fully verified across institutional accounts, hedge fund systems, and automated retail bots.

docs.title: 📦 Installation
docs.text:
Install CSharpMT5 via your standard C# package manager:

dotnet add package MetaRPC.MT5

docs.title: 🔑 API Key & Authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to MetaRPC production endpoints (mt5.mrpc.pro:443) requires an API key:

  1. Sign Up: Create an account for free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate API Key: In your MetaRPC Portal dashboard at https://mrpc.pro/my, go to API Keys to generate and copy your personal API token.
  3. Configure Connection: Pass your API key / token along with the server address (mt5.mrpc.pro:443) in your connection settings.

docs.title: 🆔 Automatic Account ID & Authentication
docs.text:
MetaRPC endpoints require authentication and session management: 1. APIKey: Your personal authentication token from https://mrpc.pro/my (obtained by registering at https://mrpc.pro/signup). Sent in the APIKey header. 2. id: A terminal session GUID returned by Connect / ConnectEx (terminalInstanceGuid).

💡 Seamless Automation: You do not need to call GetId or provide an id header when connecting. The server automatically generates a session GUID upon connection and returns it to the caller. The SDK automatically captures this session ID and attaches it alongside your APIKey to all subsequent requests and streaming subscriptions.

docs.title: 🔌 Minimal Connection Example
docs.text:
Here is how easy it is to initialize MT5Account, connect to your MetaTrader terminal, and retrieve your account balance:

// grpcServer e.g. "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443"; pass your API key (or null for env/TRIAL)
var account = new MT5Account(user, password, grpcServer, apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync(serverName, baseChartSymbol: "EURUSD", timeoutSeconds: 30);

var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance}, Equity: {summary.AccountEquity}");

await account.DisconnectAsync();

docs.title: CSharpMT5 Glossary
docs.text: Project-specific terms and concepts. This glossary covers the CSharpMT5 (C#/.NET) SDK architecture, components, and trading-automation terminology used throughout the codebase.

docs.title: Three-Tier Architecture
docs.text:
Core design pattern with three abstraction levels:

  • Tier 1 (MT5Account): Low-level gRPC communication with the MT5 terminal
  • Tier 2 (MT5Service): Wrapper methods returning plain C# types
  • Tier 3 (MT5Sugar): High-level convenience helpers with ready-made patterns
MT5Account (Low-Level)  →  Direct gRPC, proto Request/Reply
      ↓
MT5Service (Mid-Level)  →  Unwraps primitives + convenience shortcuts
      ↓
MT5Sugar  (High-Level)  →  Smart helpers, risk sizing, one-liners

docs.title: MT5Account
docs.text:
🔹 Tier 1 — Low-Level API

Base layer providing direct access to the MT5 terminal via the gRPC protocol.

Key characteristics:

  • Raw gRPC calls to the MT5 terminal
  • Works with protobuf Request/Reply objects
  • Built-in connection resilience with automatic reconnection on recoverable errors
  • Full control, maximum complexity
  • ≈45 low-level methods, each with an async and a sync variant, covering all MT5 operations
  • Returns protobuf ...Data payloads (reply.Data)
  • Session management with a terminal-instance id (GUID)

When to use: advanced users who need granular control, custom integrations, or building custom wrappers.

Location: package/Helpers/MT5Account.cs (NuGet package MetaRPC.MT5)

Documentation: MT5Account.Master.Overview.md

docs.title: MT5Service
docs.text:
🔸 Tier 2 — Wrappers API

Middle layer providing simplified method signatures without proto complexity.

Key characteristics:

  • Returns clean C# types (double, long, string, bool) where possible
  • Unwraps protobuf .Data payloads (SymbolInfoDoubleData.Value → double)
  • Simplified method names and convenience shortcuts (GetBidAsync, GetBalanceAsync, BuyMarketAsync)
  • No auto-normalization (you control precision)
  • Primary purpose: ergonomic middleware and the foundation MT5Sugar extends

When to use: building custom strategies that need more control than Sugar but less boilerplate than MT5Account.

Location: MT5Service.cs

Documentation: MT5Service.Overview.md

docs.title: MT5Sugar
docs.text:
🔺 Tier 3 — Convenience API

High-level API for common trading operations, implemented as extension methods on MT5Service.

Key characteristics:

  • Extension methods: service.PlaceMarket(...), service.BuyMarketByRisk(...)
  • Smart defaults and one-line operations
  • Risk-based position sizing (CalcVolumeForRiskAsync)
  • Friendly inputs (day windows, string timeframes, points-based pending orders)
  • Auto‑selects symbols (EnsureSelected) before acting
  • Best starting point for most use cases (~50+ helpers)

Key features:

  • PlaceMarket(symbol, volume, isBuy, sl, tp) — one call to open a position
  • CalcVolumeForRiskAsync(symbol, stopPoints, riskMoney) — volume sizing by risk
  • BuyMarketByRisk(symbol, stopPoints, riskMoney, tpPoints) — open with risk sizing
  • GetBalanceAsync(), GetEquityAsync() (from MT5Service) — account state
  • CloseAllPositions() — emergency exit

When to use: rapid development, prototyping, simple strategies, quick tools.

Location: MT5Sugar.cs

Documentation: MT5Sugar API Overview

docs.title: Async / Await
docs.text:
Every network operation is asynchronous and returns a Task / Task<T>.

using mt5_term_api;
using MetaRPC.CSharpMT5;

var account = new MT5Account(user, password, "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey: "TRIAL");
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync("MetaQuotes-Demo", "EURUSD");

// Use 'await' for all async operations
double balance = (await account.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance)); // Data.Value already unwrapped in the SDK wrapper
var positions = await account.PositionsTotalAsync();

await account.DisconnectAsync();

Sync variants. Every async method has a blocking twin (e.g. AccountSummary() vs AccountSummaryAsync()). Prefer async in 99% of cases — see Sync vs Async.

docs.title: Protobuf Data Objects
docs.text:
The low-level layer returns generated protobuf message objects, accessed via reply.Data. There are no Python-style dataclasses; you work with the generated C# types directly, or let MT5Service unwrap them.

// Low-level: returns a rich protobuf object
AccountSummaryData summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance} {summary.AccountCurrency}");

// Mid-level: unwraps to a primitive
double balance = await service.GetBalanceAsync();

Benefits of the generated types: strong typing, IDE autocomplete, and exact field parity with the proto definitions.

docs.title: Streaming — IAsyncEnumerable<T> + await foreach
docs.text:
Streaming methods return IAsyncEnumerable<T>; consume them with await foreach. Stop by breaking out of the loop or cancelling the CancellationToken.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60));

await foreach (var tickData in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
{
    var t = tickData.SymbolTick;
    Console.WriteLine($"Bid: {t.Bid}, Ask: {t.Ask}");

    if (someCondition) break; // stops the stream (auto cleanup)
}

Critical rules:

  • Use await foreach to consume the stream.
  • break ends the stream; the SDK cleans up the gRPC call.
  • Pass a CancellationToken for time-based or external cancellation.

Documentation: gRPC Stream Management

docs.title: Connection & Disposal
docs.text:
var account = new MT5Account(user, password, "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey: apiKey);

try
{
    await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync("MetaQuotes-Demo", "EURUSD");
    var service = new MT5Service(account);

    double balance = await service.GetBalanceAsync();
    var result = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", 0.01, isBuy: true);
}
finally
{
    await account.DisconnectAsync(); // sends Disconnect and disposes the gRPC channel
}

DisconnectAsync() releases the persistent gRPC connection. Always call it (e.g. in finally) to avoid resource leaks.

docs.title: Auto-Normalization
docs.text:
Automatic adjustment of trading parameters to broker requirements.

What gets normalized:

  • Volumes: rounded to the broker's volume step (e.g. 0.01 lot)
  • Prices: rounded to the symbol's tick size / digits
  • SL/TP: adjusted to symbol precision

Where: the MT5 terminal normalizes server-side; both MT5Service and MT5Sugar benefit.

Manual normalization if needed:

double step   = await service.GetVolumeStepAsync("EURUSD");
double volume = Math.Round(0.0234 / step) * step; // → 0.02 for step 0.01

long digits = await service.SymbolInfoIntegerAsync("EURUSD", SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SymbolDigits);
double price = Math.Round(1.09876543, (int)digits); // → 1.09877 for a 5-digit broker

MT5Sugar also exposes NormalizeVolumeAsync(symbol, volume).

docs.title: Risk-Based Volume Calculation
docs.text:
Calculate position size from money risk instead of a fixed lot.

Formula: volume ≈ riskMoney / (stopPoints × pointValue)

Methods (MT5Sugar):

// Volume that risks ~$5 with a 50-point stop
double volume = await service.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 50, riskMoney: 5.0);

// Open with risk sizing in one call
var result = await service.BuyMarketByRisk("EURUSD", stopPoints: 50, riskMoney: 5.0, tpPoints: 100);

Use case: consistent risk management across trades.

docs.title: Points vs Pips
docs.text:
• Point: smallest price movement for a symbol (1 tick).
  • Pip: traditional forex unit (0.0001 for most pairs).

Relationship:

  • 5-digit brokers: 1 pip = 10 points (EURUSD 1.10000 → 1.10010 = 1 pip)
  • 3-digit brokers: 1 pip = 1 point (USDJPY 110.00 → 110.01 = 1 pip)

The point-based MT5Sugar helpers (BuyLimitPoints, etc.) work in points.

double point = await service.GetPointAsync("EURUSD"); // 0.00001 for a 5-digit broker
int pointsFor20Pips = 20 * 10;                        // 5-digit pairs

docs.title: Trailing Stop
docs.text:
Dynamic Stop Loss that follows price in the profit direction.

How it works: once a position is sufficiently in profit, move the SL toward price at a fixed distance, locking in gains.

var opened = await service.OpenedOrdersAsync();
foreach (var pos in opened.PositionInfos)
{
    if (pos.Symbol != "EURUSD" || pos.Profit < 40.0) continue;

    double point = await service.GetPointAsync(pos.Symbol);
    double bid   = await service.GetBidAsync(pos.Symbol);
    double newSl = bid - 200 * point; // 20-pip trail on a 5-digit broker

    if (newSl > pos.StopLoss) // only move SL up for a BUY
        await service.ModifySlTpAsync(pos.Ticket, sl: newSl, tp: pos.TakeProfit);
}

Use case: locking in profit on trending markets.

docs.title: Breakeven
docs.text:
Moving the Stop Loss to the entry price to eliminate risk once the trade is in profit.

var opened = await service.OpenedOrdersAsync();
foreach (var pos in opened.PositionInfos)
{
    if (pos.Profit >= 40.0) // threshold in account currency
        await service.ModifySlTpAsync(pos.Ticket, sl: pos.PriceOpen, tp: pos.TakeProfit);
}

docs.title: Hedging
docs.text:
Opening an opposite position to lock the current P/L level.

var buy  = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", 0.10, isBuy: true);
// ... price moves against you ...
var sell = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", 0.10, isBuy: false); // net exposure ≈ 0

WARNING: not all brokers/regulations allow hedging (US brokers typically do not).

docs.title: Pending Order
docs.text:
An order that executes automatically when price reaches a level.

Types: BUY LIMIT (below price), SELL LIMIT (above), BUY STOP (above, breakout), SELL STOP (below, breakout).

Methods (MT5Sugar, points-based):

// Buy Limit 50 points below Ask, SL 100 / TP 200 points
await service.BuyLimitPoints("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: 50, slPoints: 100, tpPoints: 200);

// Sell Stop 50 points below Bid
await service.SellStopPoints("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: 50, slPoints: 100, tpPoints: 200);

Or build the request yourself with service.PlacePending(symbol, volume, ENUM_ORDER_TYPE.OrderTypeBuyLimit, price, sl, tp).

docs.title: Grid Trading
docs.text:
Strategy placing multiple pending orders at equal intervals above and below price. Works best in ranging markets.

int step = 20, levels = 5; // 20-pip grid
for (int i = 1; i <= levels; i++)
{
    await service.BuyLimitPoints ("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: i * step, slPoints: 150, tpPoints: 300);
    await service.SellLimitPoints("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: i * step, slPoints: 150, tpPoints: 300);
}

WARNING: high volatility can trigger many orders, increasing exposure.

docs.title: Scalping
docs.text:
Fast trading with small profits (5–25 pips) and tight stops. Needs low spreads.

await service.BuyMarketByRisk("EURUSD", stopPoints: 100, riskMoney: 5.0, tpPoints: 150);

docs.title: News Trading
docs.text:
Placing orders on both sides before a major news event, then cancelling the untriggered side.

await service.BuyStopPoints ("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: 300); // +30 pips
await service.SellStopPoints("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: 300); // -30 pips
// ... after the move, cancel the pending side you don't want:
await service.CancelAll("EURUSD");

WARNING: slippage during news can trigger both orders.

docs.title: Volume Limits
docs.text:
Broker restrictions on position size.

var (min, max, step) = await service.GetVolumeLimitsAsync("EURUSD");
double volume = Math.Clamp(requested, min, max);
volume = Math.Round(volume / step) * step; // snap to step

MT5Sugar exposes NormalizeVolumeAsync(symbol, volume) for the same effect.

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
High-performance RPC framework over HTTP/2.

In CSharpMT5:

  • MT5Account sends gRPC requests to the MT5 terminal via the gateway.
  • Request/Reply pattern for unary calls; server-streaming for On* subscriptions.
  • All calls are async.
var account = new MT5Account(user, password, "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey: apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync("MetaQuotes-Demo", "EURUSD");

Documentation: gRPC for .NET

docs.title: Protobuf
docs.text:
Protocol Buffers — Google's language-neutral serialization format.

In CSharpMT5:

  • All MT5Account methods use protobuf Request/Reply messages generated into the mt5_term_api namespace.
  • Enums and messages are strongly typed C# classes.
// Low-level returns the unwrapped primitive via the SDK wrapper
double balance = await account.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance);

// The raw reply carries reply.Data; most wrappers return .Data (or a field of it) for you
AccountSummaryData summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();

docs.title: ℹ️ Return Codes
docs.text:
Trade return codes indicating operation success/failure.

Common codes:

  • 10009 = Success (TRADE_RETCODE_DONE)
  • 10008 = Pending order placed (TRADE_RETCODE_PLACED)
  • 10004 = Requote · 10006 = Rejected · 10013 = Invalid request
  • 10014 = Invalid volume · 10015 = Invalid price · 10016 = Invalid stops
  • 10018 = Market closed · 10019 = Not enough money · 10031 = No connection to trade server
var result = await account.OrderSendAsync(request);

if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    Console.WriteLine($"Trade done! Order: {result.Order}");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"Trade failed: {result.ReturnedCode} ({result.ReturnedCodeDescription})");

Documentation: Return Codes Reference

docs.title: 📡 Streaming Pattern
docs.text:
Real-time data via IAsyncEnumerable<T>.

// Ticks
await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, ct))
    Console.WriteLine($"Bid: {td.SymbolTick.Bid}, Ask: {td.SymbolTick.Ask}");

// Trade events
await foreach (var ev in account.OnTradeAsync(ct))
    Console.WriteLine($"Trade event: {ev.Type}");

// Position profit (poll every 500 ms)
await foreach (var p in account.OnPositionProfitAsync(intervalMs: 500, cancellationToken: ct))
    foreach (var pos in p.UpdatedPositions)
        Console.WriteLine($"Ticket {pos.Ticket}: {pos.Profit}");

Documentation: gRPC Stream Management

docs.title: Basic Trading Terms
docs.text:
Core concepts every trader should know before working with MT5.

Term Description Example / Details Bid Price at which the broker buys from you (you sell at Bid) EURUSD Bid: 1.10000 Ask Price at which the broker sells to you (you buy at Ask) EURUSD Ask: 1.10002 Spread Difference between Ask and Bid Ask 1.10002 − Bid 1.10000 = 2 pips Long / Buy BUY position (profit when price rises) Buy 1.10000, close 1.10050 = +50 pips Short / Sell SELL position (profit when price falls) Sell 1.10000, close 1.09950 = +50 pips Position Open trade that can profit or lose BUY 0.1 lot EURUSD at 1.10000 Order Command to open a position Market (immediate) or Pending (at a price) Market Order Executes immediately at current price BUY EURUSD at Ask Pending Order Triggers when price reaches a level BUY LIMIT at 1.09950 Lot / Volume Position size (1 lot = 100,000 base units) 0.01 lot = 1,000 units (micro) Stop Loss (SL) Auto loss-limiting exit level SL 1.09950 limits loss to 50 pips Take Profit (TP) Auto profit-taking exit level TP 1.10050 locks 50 pips Pip Standard unit of movement (0.0001 for most forex) 1.10000 → 1.10001 = 1 pip Point Smallest movement (1 tick) 5-digit broker: 1 pip = 10 points Leverage Borrowed capital (e.g. 1:100) $1,000 margin controls $100,000 Margin Collateral locked for open positions 1 lot EURUSD @ 1:100 ≈ $1,000 margin Free Margin Funds available for new positions Balance − Margin Balance Funds excluding open positions Deposit + realized P/L Equity Balance ± floating P/L $10,000 + $500 floating = $10,500 Floating P/L Unrealized P/L of open positions Position currently +$50 Margin Level Equity / Margin (%) $10,500 / $1,000 = 1050% Margin Call Warning when Margin Level drops low e.g. at 100% Stop Out Forced close when Margin Level critical e.g. at 50% Drawdown Decline from peak balance/equity Peak 11,000 → 10,000 = 9.09% Slippage Expected vs executed price difference Requested 1.10000, filled 1.10003

Critical for API usage:

// Prices
double bid = await service.GetBidAsync("EURUSD");
double ask = await service.GetAskAsync("EURUSD");

// Account state
double balance    = await service.GetBalanceAsync();
double equity     = await service.GetEquityAsync();
double freeMargin = await service.GetFreeMarginAsync();

// Open / modify / close
var buy = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", 0.01, isBuy: true);
if (buy.Order > 0)
{
    await service.ModifySlTpAsync(buy.Order, sl: 1.09950, tp: 1.10050);
    await service.CloseByTicket(buy.Order);
}

docs.title: Risk Amount
docs.text:
The money you are willing to lose if the Stop Loss hits.

// Volume that risks ~$5 with a 50-point stop, then open with it
double volume = await service.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 50, riskMoney: 5.0);
var result = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", volume, isBuy: true);

docs.title: appsettings.json
docs.text:
The examples read connection settings from Config/appsettings.json.

{
  "MT5": {
    "User": 5056776453,
    "Password": "...",
    "ServerName": "MetaQuotes-Demo",
    "GrpcServer": "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443",
    "ApiKey": "mrpc_live_...",
    "ConnectTimeoutSeconds": 60
  }
}

Loaded via ConnectionHelper.BuildConfiguration() / CreateAndConnectAccountAsync(config).

docs.title: Environment variable override
docs.text:
MRPC_API_KEY overrides the config API key at runtime (useful for not committing a real key):

$env:MRPC_API_KEY = "TRIAL"   # or your account key
dotnet run lowlevel

WARNING: never commit real credentials. Keep live keys out of source control.

docs.title: Batch Operations
docs.text:
Acting on many positions/orders at once (MT5Sugar):

int closed    = await service.CloseAllPositions();          // all positions
int closedEur = await service.CloseAllPositions("EURUSD");  // by symbol
int cancelled = await service.CancelAll();                  // all pending orders

Use case: emergency exits, end-of-session cleanup, strategy resets.

docs.title: 📝 History Queries
docs.text:
Retrieving past orders/positions for analysis (MT5Account / MT5Service).

var from = DateTime.UtcNow.AddDays(-30);
var to   = DateTime.UtcNow;

// Orders (paged)
var orders = await service.OrderHistoryAsync(from, to,
    BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE.Bmt5SortByCloseTimeDesc, pageNumber: 0, itemsPerPage: 100);

// Full order history in one call
var all = await service.AllHistoryOrdersAsync(from, to);

// Closed positions
var positions = await service.PositionsHistoryAsync(
    AH_ENUM_POSITIONS_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE.AhPositionOpenTimeDesc, openFrom: from, openTo: to, page: 0, size: 100);

Friendly Sugar forms: OrdersHistoryLast(days), AllHistoryOrdersLast(days), PositionsHistoryPaged(...).

docs.title: Educational Project
docs.text:
The CSharpMT5 examples, orchestrators and helpers are educational materials and API demonstrations, not production trading systems.

Implications:

  • Study code and patterns ✅
  • Modify for your needs ✅
  • Test on demo accounts ✅
  • Use as templates for your own strategies ✅
  • Do not run as-is with real money ❌
  • Do not expect production-grade risk management or exhaustive error handling ❌

docs.title: 🧱 Enums
docs.text:
The SDK uses generated protobuf enums instead of magic numbers. They live in the mt5_term_api namespace; the C# member is PascalCase (its proto OriginalName is the SCREAMING_SNAKE form).

using mt5_term_api;

double bid = await service.SymbolInfoDoubleAsync("EURUSD", SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.SymbolBid);
double bal = await account.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance);

var req = new OrderSendRequest
{
    Symbol = "EURUSD",
    Operation = TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE.Tmt5OrderTypeBuy
};

docs.title: gRPC Streaming and Subscription Management Guide
docs.text:
Complete guide to working with real-time subscriptions in CSharpMT5 (C# / .NET).

This document covers:

  • ✅ How to subscribe properly to market-data streams
  • ✅ How to stop subscriptions without leaking the gRPC call
  • ✅ Common patterns from simple to advanced
  • ✅ Architecture and built-in safety mechanisms
  • ✅ Troubleshooting and best practices

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Quick Start
  2. Available Streaming Methods
  3. Complete Patterns
  4. Why Streams Need Management
  5. Best Practices
  6. Advanced Examples with Enums
  7. Multiple Concurrent Streams
  8. Architecture and Safety
  9. Troubleshooting

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: In C# every streaming method returns an IAsyncEnumerable<T> that you consume with await foreach. The stream advances only while you consume it, so stopping consumption (a break, or cancelling the token) stops the stream.

docs.title: 1️⃣ Simplest pattern — stop after N events
docs.text:
using mt5_term_api;
using MetaRPC.CSharpMT5;

var account = new MT5Account(user, password, "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync("YourBroker-Demo", "EURUSD");

try
{
    int count = 0;
    await foreach (var tickData in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD" }))
    {
        var t = tickData.SymbolTick;
        Console.WriteLine($"[{++count}] Bid={t.Bid:F5}, Ask={t.Ask:F5}");

        if (count >= 10) break; // stops the stream; the enumerator is disposed → gRPC call cancelled
    }
}
finally
{
    await account.DisconnectAsync();
}

When to use: quick examples, testing, short monitoring sessions.

docs.title: 2️⃣ Auto-timeout — CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan)
docs.text:
A break only runs when the next message arrives. To stop a quiet stream after a fixed time, drive it with a cancellation token:

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)); // auto-cancels after 10s

try
{
    await foreach (var tickData in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine($"Bid={tickData.SymbolTick.Bid:F5}");
}
catch (OperationCanceledException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Stream stopped (timeout)");
}
finally
{
    await account.DisconnectAsync();
}

docs.title: 3️⃣ Manual control — cancel from elsewhere
docs.text:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();

// Run the stream in the background
var monitor = Task.Run(async () =>
{
    await foreach (var tickData in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine($"Price: {tickData.SymbolTick.Bid:F5}");
});

// ... do other work ...
await Task.Delay(5000);
cts.Cancel();                 // signal the stream to stop
try { await monitor; } catch (OperationCanceledException) { }

await account.DisconnectAsync();

When to use: long-term monitoring, background services, production apps.

docs.title: MT5Account (low-level streams)
docs.text:
All streaming methods return an IAsyncEnumerable<T> and accept a CancellationToken.

Method Description Yields OnSymbolTickAsync(symbols, ct) Real-time price ticks OnSymbolTickData OnTradeAsync(ct) Trade events (orders created/changed/closed) OnTradeData OnPositionProfitAsync(intervalMs, ignoreEmpty, ct) Position P&L updates (polled) OnPositionProfitData OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsAsync(intervalMs, ct) Position/pending ticket snapshots OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData OnTradeTransactionAsync(ct) Low-level trade transaction events OnTradeTransactionData

Documentation: - Streaming Methods Overview - SubscribeToTicks · OnTrade · SubscribeToPositionProfit

Examples: Examples/LowLevel/Program.Streaming.cs, and the Sugar helpers ReadTicks / ReadTrades (Examples/Sugar/Program.Sugar.cs).

docs.title: Pattern 1 — Quick example (count + timeout)
docs.text:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
try
{
    int count = 0;
    await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Tick #{++count}: {td.SymbolTick.Bid:F5}");
        if (count >= 5) break;
    }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { /* timed out */ }
finally { await account.DisconnectAsync(); }

docs.title: Pattern 2 — Event-limited streaming
docs.text:
const int maxEvents = 100;
int count = 0;
await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{++count}] {td.SymbolTick.Bid:F5}");
    if (count >= maxEvents) break;
}

docs.title: Pattern 3 — Condition-based stop
docs.text:
await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }))
{
    double bid = td.SymbolTick.Bid;
    Console.WriteLine($"Price: {bid:F5}");
    if (bid > 1.10000) { Console.WriteLine("Target reached!"); break; }
}

docs.title: Pattern 4 — Background service with manual control
docs.text:
public sealed class PriceMonitor
{
    private readonly MT5Account _account;
    private readonly CancellationTokenSource _cts = new();
    private Task? _task;

    public PriceMonitor(MT5Account account) => _account = account;

    public void Start(IEnumerable<string> symbols) =>
        _task = Task.Run(() => MonitorAsync(symbols, _cts.Token));

    private async Task MonitorAsync(IEnumerable<string> symbols, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            await foreach (var td in _account.OnSymbolTickAsync(symbols, ct))
                Console.WriteLine($"{td.SymbolTick.Bid:F5} / {td.SymbolTick.Ask:F5}");
        }
        catch (OperationCanceledException) { /* expected on stop */ }
    }

    public async Task StopAsync()
    {
        _cts.Cancel();
        if (_task is not null) { try { await _task; } catch (OperationCanceledException) { } }
    }
}

// Usage
var monitor = new PriceMonitor(account);
monitor.Start(new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD" });
await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
await monitor.StopAsync();
await account.DisconnectAsync();

docs.title: Why Streams Need Management
docs.text:
A streaming subscription is a live gRPC server-stream. Two things matter:

  1. The stream is consumer-driven. The underlying loop only advances when your await foreach asks for the next item. When you break (or the loop ends), the async enumerator is disposed and the SDK cancels the current gRPC call in its finally. So break is enough to stop the stream — there is no orphaned background task as in some other runtimes.

  2. A blocked wait needs a token to interrupt it. If no new message is arriving, await foreach is parked inside MoveNextAsync and your break/condition cannot run yet. Pass a CancellationToken (from a CancellationTokenSource) so you can interrupt that wait — on cancel, MoveNextAsync throws OperationCanceledException, the enumerator is disposed, and the stream ends.

// ❌ Can't stop a quiet stream promptly — nothing interrupts the wait:
await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }))
{
    if (DateTime.UtcNow > deadline) break; // only checked when a tick arrives
}

// ✅ Token interrupts the wait immediately:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));
try
{
    await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token)) { /* ... */ }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }

Rule of thumb: use break for event/condition limits; add a CancellationToken whenever you need a time limit or external stop, or whenever the stream may go quiet.

docs.title: ✅ DO
docs.text:
1. Consume every stream with await foreach.
  2. Pass a CancellationToken for time limits or external cancellation.
  3. Wrap token-driven loops in try { … } catch (OperationCanceledException) { }.
  4. Always break (or cancel) when you have what you need — don't loop forever by accident.
  5. Call await account.DisconnectAsync() in a finally to release the channel when you're done with the account.
  6. Share one CancellationTokenSource across several streams to stop them together.

docs.title: ❌ DON'T
docs.text:
1. Don't rely on a break alone to stop a stream that may be quiet — add a token.
  2. Don't forget catch (OperationCanceledException) when you cancel via a token (otherwise it surfaces as an error).
  3. Don't Dispose() the MT5Account/channel while a stream is still iterating — stop the stream first.
  4. Don't swallow real stream errors (RpcException, ApiExceptionMT5) — only the cancellation is expected.

docs.title: Example 1 — Filter trade transactions by type
docs.text:
using mt5_term_api;

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
try
{
    await foreach (var data in account.OnTradeTransactionAsync(cts.Token))
    {
        var tx = data.TradeTransaction;
        if (tx is null) continue;

        switch (tx.Type)
        {
            case SUB_ENUM_TRADE_TRANSACTION_TYPE.SubTradeTransactionOrderAdd:
                Console.WriteLine($"[NEW ORDER] #{tx.OrderTicket} {tx.Symbol} ({tx.OrderType})");
                break;
            case SUB_ENUM_TRADE_TRANSACTION_TYPE.SubTradeTransactionOrderDelete:
                Console.WriteLine($"[ORDER DELETED] #{tx.OrderTicket}");
                break;
            case SUB_ENUM_TRADE_TRANSACTION_TYPE.SubTradeTransactionDealAdd:
                Console.WriteLine($"[NEW DEAL] deal #{tx.DealTicket} order #{tx.OrderTicket} {tx.Symbol}");
                break;
        }
    }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
finally { await account.DisconnectAsync(); }

docs.title: Example 2 — Positions sorted by profit
docs.text:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1));
try
{
    await foreach (var p in account.OnPositionProfitAsync(intervalMs: 1000, ignoreEmpty: true, cancellationToken: cts.Token))
    {
        var positions = p.UpdatedPositions.OrderByDescending(x => x.Profit).ToList();
        if (positions.Count == 0) continue;

        double total = positions.Sum(x => x.Profit);
        int winners  = positions.Count(x => x.Profit > 0);

        Console.WriteLine($"\n[UPDATE] {positions.Count} positions | Total {total:+0.00;-0.00} | Winners {winners}");
        foreach (var pos in positions.Take(5))
            Console.WriteLine($"  {pos.PositionSymbol,-10} #{pos.Ticket,-10} {pos.Profit,10:F2}");
    }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
finally { await account.DisconnectAsync(); }

Enum/field names come straight from the generated proto types in the mt5_term_api namespace — see Enums Usage Reference.

docs.title: Multiple Concurrent Streams
docs.text:
Run several streams at once and stop them all with one token via Task.WhenAll.

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)); // auto-stop all after 30s

async Task StreamTicks()
{
    try { await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine($"[TICK] {td.SymbolTick.Bid:F5}"); }
    catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
}

async Task StreamTrades()
{
    try { await foreach (var ev in account.OnTradeAsync(cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine($"[TRADE] {ev.Type}"); }
    catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
}

async Task StreamProfits()
{
    try { await foreach (var p in account.OnPositionProfitAsync(2000, true, cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine($"[PROFIT] {p.UpdatedPositions.Count} positions updated"); }
    catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
}

try
{
    await Task.WhenAll(StreamTicks(), StreamTrades(), StreamProfits());
}
finally
{
    await account.DisconnectAsync();
    Console.WriteLine("[DONE] all streams stopped");
}

A single cts.Cancel() (or the timeout) stops every stream that shares the token.

docs.title: How streaming works inside MT5Account
docs.text:
All streaming methods (OnSymbolTickAsync, OnTradeAsync, OnPositionProfitAsync, OnTradeTransactionAsync, OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsAsync) share the same internal helper: ExecuteStreamWithReconnect.

Data flow:

Your code (await foreach)
    ↓ pulls items
ExecuteStreamWithReconnect  (reconnect loop + error handling)
    ↓
gRPC server stream  →  Network  →  MT5 terminal

Simplified structure (C#):

private async IAsyncEnumerable<TData> ExecuteStreamWithReconnect<...>(
    TRequest request, ...,
    [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    while (!cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested)
    {
        bool reconnectRequired = false;
        AsyncServerStreamingCall<TReply> stream = null;
        try
        {
            stream = streamInvoker(request, GetHeaders(), cancellationToken);
            while (await stream.ResponseStream.MoveNext(cancellationToken))
            {
                var error = getError(stream.ResponseStream.Current);
                if (error?.ErrorCode is "TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND" or "TERMINAL_REGISTRY_TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND")
                { reconnectRequired = true; break; }
                if (error != null) throw new ApiExceptionMT5(error);

                var data = getData(stream.ResponseStream.Current);
                if (data != null) yield return data;   // ← handed to your await foreach
            }
        }
        catch (RpcException ex) when ((int)ex.StatusCode == 14 /* UNAVAILABLE */)
        {
            reconnectRequired = true;
        }
        finally
        {
            stream?.Dispose();                           // ✅ always closes the current gRPC stream
        }

        if (!reconnectRequired) break;                   // normal end
        await Task.Delay(500, cancellationToken);
        await Reconnect(null, cancellationToken);         // transient network error → reconnect
    }
}

What it does:

  • ✅ Disposes the current gRPC stream automatically (finally).
  • ✅ Reconnects transparently on a recoverable network error (StatusCode 14, UNAVAILABLE) and on TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND.
  • ✅ Surfaces real API errors as ApiExceptionMT5.

What you control:

  • The loop runs while the consumer keeps pulling and the token isn't cancelled. Because it's an iterator, it does not run on its own in the background — stop consuming (break) or cancel the token and it ends. Then call DisconnectAsync() to release the channel.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Stream never stops on a quiet market Relying on break/condition only; the wait is parked Pass a CancellationToken (e.g. new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan…)) OperationCanceledException bubbles up as an error You cancelled via token but didn't catch it Wrap the loop in try { … } catch (OperationCanceledException) { } RpcException StatusCode Unavailable mid-stream Transient network drop Handled automatically — the SDK reconnects; no action needed ObjectDisposedException on the channel Account/channel disposed while a stream still iterates Stop the stream first, then DisconnectAsync() Stream ends immediately with an API error Real server error (e.g. not connected) Inspect the ApiExceptionMT5 message; ensure you connected first

docs.title: Verifying a stream stopped
docs.text:
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
var task = Task.Run(async () =>
{
    try { await foreach (var td in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token)) { } }
    catch (OperationCanceledException) { }
});

await Task.Delay(2000);
cts.Cancel();
await task;                      // completes once the stream has unwound
Console.WriteLine("Stream fully stopped");

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• Streaming Methods Overview — all streaming methods
  • SubscribeToTicks — tick streaming reference
  • OnTrade — trade-events reference
  • Enums Usage Reference — enum types used in stream payloads
  • Sync vs Async — async patterns in the SDK
  • gRPC for .NET — official .NET gRPC docs

Remember: C# streams are consumer-driven — break stops them, and a CancellationToken lets you interrupt a quiet wait or stop from outside. Catch OperationCanceledException, disconnect when done, and your streaming code stays robust and leak-free. 🚀

docs.title: MT5 for Beginners: Your First Steps in Trading
docs.text: Welcome! This guide is designed for complete beginners who have never worked with MetaTrader 5 or trading. We'll walk you through everything you need to know to get started.

docs.title: What is MetaTrader 5 (MT5)?
docs.text:
MetaTrader 5 is a powerful trading platform used by millions of traders worldwide. It allows you to:

  • Trade forex, stocks, commodities, and cryptocurrencies
  • Analyze markets with charts and indicators
  • Execute automated trading strategies
  • Monitor your positions in real-time

Think of MT5 as your "cockpit" for accessing financial markets. CSharpMT5 lets you programmatically control this cockpit from C# / .NET.

docs.title: Demo vs Live Account: Start Safely
Why start with a demo account?
docs.text:
A demo account is a risk-free practice account with virtual money. We strongly recommend starting with demo for several reasons:

  • ✅ Zero risk - practice with virtual funds (typically $10,000 - $100,000)
  • ✅ Real market conditions - live prices and market behavior
  • ✅ Learn the platform - understand how MT5 works before risking real money
  • ✅ Test your code - perfect for developing and testing your CSharpMT5 applications

docs.title: Live Account
docs.text:
A live account uses your real money. Only move to live trading when you:

  • Understand how MT5 works
  • Have thoroughly tested your strategies on demo
  • Are aware of the risks involved

docs.title: Quick Start: Creating a Demo Account
docs.text: The fastest way to get started is to create a demo account directly through the MT5 terminal application.

docs.title: Step 1️⃣: Download and Install MT5 Terminal
docs.text:
1. Visit the official MetaTrader website: https://www.metatrader5.com/en/download

  2. Download the version for your operating system (Windows/Mac/Linux)

  3. Install the application

docs.title: Step 2️⃣: Launch MT5 and Locate the Navigator Panel
docs.text:
When you open the MetaTrader 5 application, you'll typically see a popup window offering to:

  • Register for the MQL community

  • Open a new account or log into an existing one

If this popup doesn't appear automatically, you need to find the Navigator panel.

Finding the Navigator Panel:

The Navigator panel is usually located on the left side of the screen, below the Market Watch panel.

Inside the Navigator panel you'll see several sections: - Accounts - Subscriptions - Indicators - Expert Advisors - And others

docs.title: Step 3️⃣: Opening a New Demo Account
docs.text:
1. In the Navigator panel, find the Accounts section
  2. Right-click on "Accounts"
  3. Select "Open an account" from the context menu

This will open the broker server search panel.

docs.title: Step 4️⃣: Select MetaQuotes Demo Server
docs.text:
In the broker search window, you'll see a list of available MT5 servers.

For your first demo account, we'll use the simplest option:

  • Look for "MetaQuotes-Demo" or "MetaQuotes Ltd" in the list
  • This is the standard demo server provided by MetaTrader developers
  • If you don't see it immediately, use the search field at the top to find it

Select the MetaQuotes server and click Next.

docs.title: Step 5️⃣: Account Type Selection
docs.text:
On the next screen, you'll have options:

  • Open a new demo account (top option)
  • Log into an existing account (demo or live)

Select "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

docs.title: Step 6️⃣: Fill in Your Personal Information
docs.text:
Now you'll see a form requesting your details:

  • Name: Your first name
  • Last Name: Your last name
  • Email: Your email address
  • Phone: Optional (can skip for demo)
  • Account Type: Choose your preferred account settings
  • Deposit: Virtual amount (e.g., $10,000)
  • Leverage: 1:100 is a good starting point
  • Currency: USD, EUR, etc.

Check the box to agree to the terms and conditions, then click Next.

docs.title: Step 7️⃣: Save Your Account Credentials
docs.text:
MT5 will now create your demo account and display your credentials:

Important credentials displayed:

  • Login: Your account number (e.g., 591129415)
  • Password: Your master password for trading
  • Investor Password: Read-only password (for monitoring)
  • Server: Server name (e.g., "MetaQuotes-Demo")

⚠️ CRITICALLY IMPORTANT: Save these credentials immediately! You'll need them for: - Logging back into MT5 - Configuring CSharpMT5 in Config/appsettings.json

Click Finish to complete account creation.

docs.title: Step 8️⃣: Configure CSharpMT5 with Your Credentials
docs.text:
Now that you have an MT5 demo account, you need to configure CSharpMT5 to connect to it.

  1. Open the CSharpMT5 project
  2. Navigate to Config/appsettings.json
  3. Fill in the credentials you just saved:
{
  "MT5": {
    "User": 591129415,
    "Password": "YourPasswordHere",
    "ServerName": "MetaQuotes-Demo",
    "GrpcServer": "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443",
    "ApiKey": "your-api-key",
    "ConnectTimeoutSeconds": 60
  }
}

Important notes:

  • User: replace with your login number
  • Password: replace with your password
  • ServerName: the exact server name from MT5 (e.g., "MetaQuotes-Demo")
  • GrpcServer: the MetaRPC gateway address (leave as is)
  • ApiKey: your MetaRPC key — or set the MRPC_API_KEY environment variable instead of committing it (use TRIAL for trial access)

docs.title: Step 9️⃣: Verify MT5 Connection
docs.text:
Back in the MT5 terminal:

  1. MT5 should automatically log you into your new demo account
  2. Check the bottom right corner of the terminal window - you should see:
  3. Green connection indicator (means connected to server)
  4. Your account balance (e.g., $10,000)

You're now ready to test!

docs.title: Step 🔟: Start Testing CSharpMT5
docs.text:
With your MT5 demo account created and Config/appsettings.json configured, you can start running examples:

# From the project root
dotnet run lowlevel      # run the low-level info demo
dotnet run trading       # run the trading demo
dotnet run service       # run the MT5Service demo
dotnet run sugar         # run the MT5Sugar demo

When trading operations occur, your demo account balance will increase or decrease accordingly. Experiment freely - it's virtual money, so there's no risk!

All trades executed by CSharpMT5 will appear in your MT5 terminal in real-time.

docs.title: 🧩 Understanding MT5 Password Types
docs.text: MT5 uses two types of passwords for security and flexibility:

docs.title: Master Password (Main Password)
docs.text:
• Full access to your trading account
  • Can open/close trades, deposit/withdraw funds, change settings
  • This is the password you created during account registration
  • Use this password for:
  • Trading (including CSharpMT5 applications)
  • Changing account settings
  • Withdrawing funds (live accounts)

docs.title: Investor Password (Read-Only Password)
docs.text:
• View-only access to your account
  • Can see trades, balance, history - but cannot trade
  • Useful for:
  • Sharing your trading performance with others (investors, friends)
  • Monitoring your account without risk
  • Audit and analytics tools

How to get your investor password:

  1. In MT5, go to Tools → Options
  2. Select the Server tab
  3. Click Change next to "Investor Password"
  4. Set a new investor password

docs.title: Choosing a Broker (Optional)
docs.text:
While you can use the MetaQuotes demo server for practice, you may want to choose a specific broker for:

  • Live trading later
  • Better demo conditions (spreads, instruments)
  • Specific regional support

docs.title: Popular MT5 Brokers:
docs.text:
Note: This is not financial advice. Always do your own research before choosing a broker.

  • IC Markets - Popular for forex and low spreads
  • Pepperstone - Well-regulated, beginner-friendly
  • OANDA - Strong reputation, accepts US clients
  • XM - Easy account opening, many account types
  • RoboForex - Good for automated trading
  • FxPro - Excellent demo trading conditions

docs.title: What to look for:
docs.text:
• ✅ Regulation - Check if regulated by FCA, ASIC, CySEC, etc.

  • ✅ MT5 Support - Make sure they offer MT5 (not just MT4).

  • ✅ Demo Account - Free demo without expiration (though demo accounts typically last 30 days, then become inactive).

  • ✅ Good Spreads - Lower spreads = lower trading costs.

  • ✅ Customer Support - Responsive support in your language.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text: Now that you have a demo account and understand the basics, you're ready for:

docs.title: 1. Setting Up CSharpMT5
docs.text:
Follow our main getting started guide to connect CSharpMT5 to your MT5 account:

👉 Getting Started with CSharpMT5

docs.title: 2. Understanding API Architecture
docs.text: CSharpMT5 is built in three levels, from low-level to high-level. You can choose where to start depending on your needs:

docs.title: Level 1: MT5Account (Low-Level gRPC Foundation)
docs.text:
👉 MT5Account Overview

  • Direct gRPC calls to MT5 terminal
  • Foundation of everything - all other levels use this internally
  • Maximum control and flexibility
  • Best for: Advanced users who need fine-grained control

docs.title: Level 2: MT5Service (Convenient Wrappers)
docs.text:
👉 MT5Service Overview

  • Wrapper methods over MT5Account gRPC calls
  • Simplified error handling and response parsing
  • Easier to work with than raw gRPC
  • Best for: Most common trading scenarios

docs.title: Level 3: MT5Sugar (High-Level Helpers)
docs.text:
👉 MT5Sugar API Overview

  • Syntactic sugar and convenience methods
  • Chainable operations, smart defaults
  • Most intuitive and beginner-friendly
  • Best for: Rapid prototyping and simple strategies

docs.title: 🛡️ Security
docs.text:
• Never share your master password with anyone
  • Use investor password for monitoring/analytics tools
  • Keep your credentials safe (use password managers)

docs.title: 📊 Risk Management
docs.text:
• Demo accounts are risk-free, but form good habits:
  • Always use Stop Loss
  • Don't risk more than 1-2% per trade
  • Understand position sizing calculations

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text:
• Test all your CSharpMT5 code on demo first
  • Verify strategies over weeks/months, not days
  • Paper trading (demo) doesn't guarantee live results

docs.title: 📚 Education
docs.text:
• Trading has a steep learning curve
  • Focus on learning, not earning
  • Consider courses, books, and communities

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Add the CSharpMT5 package to your project
dotnet add package MetaRPC.MT5

docs.title: Running Examples
docs.text:
# From the project root
dotnet run lowlevel   # low-level MT5Account demo
dotnet run service    # MT5Service demo
dotnet run sugar      # MT5Sugar demo
dotnet run trading    # trading lifecycle demo

docs.title: Checking Environment
docs.text:
# Verify the .NET SDK (this project targets .NET 8)
dotnet --version

Ready to start coding? Head over to Getting Started to connect CSharpMT5 to your MT5 account!

Good luck with your trading journey! 🚀

docs.title: 🗺️ CSharpMT5 Project Map
docs.text: The whole project as one annotated tree, with links. Links point to section overviews, never to individual method pages — open an overview to drill down into its methods.

docs.title: 🧱 The three layers
docs.text:
CSharpMT5 is built in three decoupled layers. Your code can enter at any level.

Layer Source What it does Overview 3 · MT5Sugar MT5Sugar.cs Convenience on top of Service (extension methods): points-based SL/TP, risk-based sizing, price/volume normalization, snapshots, batch close/cancel, market-data & stats helpers. MT5Sugar overview 2 · MT5Service MT5Service.cs Typed facade: friendly signatures, unwrapped C# primitives (no raw proto), convenience shortcuts (GetBidAsync, BuyMarketAsync). What most code uses. MT5Service overview 1 · MT5Account package/Helpers/MT5Account.cs Low-level gRPC: proto request/reply, connect/session, auto-reconnect, streaming. Everything else builds on it. MT5Account overview 
Your code  →  MT5Sugar  →  MT5Service  →  MT5Account  →  gRPC  →  MetaRPC gateway → MT5 terminal

    • MetaRPC.MT5.csproj — the publishable package project
  • Errors/ — domain exceptions: ApiExceptionMT5.cs, ConnectExceptionMT5.cs
  • Examples/ — runnable demos (dispatched by Program.cs)

    • LowLevel/ — Program.LowLevel / .Trading / .Streaming → MT5Account overview

docs.text:

  • Home — landing page

docs.title: 🎯 Which layer should you use?
docs.text:
• Most trading apps → MT5Sugar. Points-based SL/TP, risk sizing and auto-normalization protect you from off-quote and invalid-volume rejections.
  • Custom execution → MT5Service. Typed calls when you manage your own sizing/normalization.
  • Protocol-level control → MT5Account. Raw proto structures and streams.

docs.title: Protobuf Inspector — Interactive Type Explorer
docs.text: Interactive developer utility for exploring the MetaRPC.MT5 protobuf types, fields and enums of the MT5 gRPC API — straight from the compiled C# assembly.

docs.title: 🏛️ What this tool does
docs.text:
The Protobuf Inspector is an interactive console tool that reflects over the generated mt5_term_api C# types so you can explore the API without a terminal connection:

  • Interactive search for types, fields and enums
  • Inspect a message type and see its C# properties and their types
  • Field-level discovery — find which types contain a given field
  • Enum value exploration — list all values of an enum
  • Type browsing — list all available types

It reads C# property names (PascalCase), e.g. AccountSummaryData.AccountBalance, not the proto wire names.

docs.title: Running the inspector
docs.text:
dotnet run inspect

You'll see a header, a quick-start box, and an interactive prompt:

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║          🔍 INTERACTIVE PROTOBUF TYPES INSPECTOR 🔍                ║
║         Explore MT5 gRPC API Types, Fields & Enums                ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Assembly: MetaRPC.CSharpMT5 v1.0.0.0

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ QUICK START GUIDE                                              │
│ • Type 'help' for full command list                            │
│ • Type 'list' to see all available types                       │
│ • Type a type name to inspect it (e.g., 'OpenedOrdersData')    │
│ • Type 'exit' to quit                                          │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

>

docs.title: 🧰 Available Commands
docs.text:
Command Description Example list or ls Show all available protobuf types (Data / Request / Reply) list <TypeName> Inspect a type — shows its properties and their types OpenedOrdersData search <text> or find <text> Search for types whose name contains the text search Order field <name> Find all types that contain a field field Ticket enum <name> Show all values of an enum enum BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE help or ? Show the help message help exit, quit or q Exit the inspector exit

Search and type names are case-insensitive.

docs.title: "Getting a wrong-property error"
docs.text:
Problem: your code has summary.Ballance but it won't compile.

> AccountSummaryData
→ shows the correct property is AccountBalance.

docs.title: "What data is in X?"
docs.text:
> OpenedOrdersData
→ lists every property and its type (e.g. PositionInfos, OpenedOrders).

docs.title: "What enum value do I pass?"
docs.text:
> enum ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF
→ shows OrderTypeTfBuy = 0, OrderTypeTfSell = 1, …

docs.title: "Which type holds this field?"
docs.text:
> field Profit
→ shows PositionInfo, OnPositionProfitPositionInfo, … (substring match, so it also finds related fields).

docs.title: "Just exploring the API"
docs.text:
> list
→ browse all available types, then inspect any by name.

docs.title: Frequently used enums
docs.text:
Enum Context Notes ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF Trade functions (OrderCalcMargin, OrderCalcProfit, OrderCheck) OrderTypeTfBuy, OrderTypeTfSell, … (9 values) TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE OrderSend / OrderSendWithoutChecks request operation Tmt5OrderTypeBuy, … (9 values) TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME Order lifetime GTC / Day / Specified (4 values) BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE History orders order type in HistoryOrderInfo BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE OrderHistory / AllHistoryOrders sort 6 values SUB_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE, SUB_ENUM_ORDER_STATE, SUB_ENUM_DEAL_TYPE Streaming events (OnTrade, OnTradeTransaction) the SUB_ENUM_* family SymbolInfoDoubleProperty SymbolInfoDouble selector 60 values (BID, ASK, POINT, …) SymbolInfoIntegerProperty SymbolInfoInteger selector 37 values AccountInfoDoublePropertyType AccountInfoDouble selector 14 values

Prefix meaning:

  • TMT5_* — trading-helper request enums (OrderSend)
  • ENUM_*_TF — trade-functions enums (margin/profit/check)
  • BMT5_* — base MT5 enums (history, symbol params)
  • SUB_* — subscription/streaming enums (real-time events)

Full tables: Enums Usage Reference.

docs.title: Technical Notes
docs.text:
• No MT5 connection required — the inspector reflects over the compiled mt5_term_api assembly; it never connects to a terminal.
  • C# names — it reports C# property and enum-member names (PascalCase), which is exactly what you write in code.
  • Development only — a utility for exploring the API, not for production use.
  • Source file: Examples/Helpers/ProtobufInspector.cs (entry point ProtobufInspector.Run(), invoked by dotnet run inspect).

docs.title: When to use this tool
docs.text:
Use it when:

  • Learning the MT5 gRPC API structure
  • Debugging a wrong property/field name
  • Looking up enum values before building a request
  • Finding the right Request/Reply/Data type for a call
  • Understanding a message's shape before writing code

Don't use it for:

  • Inspecting runtime data (use the debugger)
  • Production code (it's a dev utility)
  • Testing connectivity (use a demo connection)

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. Start with search when you know the general area (search Position).
  2. Use field <name> when you see a field but don't know its type.
  3. Explore enums early — enum <name> saves debugging time later.
  4. list when stuck — browse everything, then inspect by name.
  5. Case doesn't matter — type commands and names in any case.

docs.title: Command Quick Reference
docs.text:
list / ls          - show all types
  <TypeName>         - inspect a type's properties
  search <text>      - find types by name (alias: find)
  field <name>       - find types containing a field
  enum <name>        - show enum values
  help / ?           - show help
  exit / quit / q    - exit

docs.title: 🛡️ What is RetCode?
docs.text:
RetCode (Return Code) is a status code the MT5 terminal returns after a trading operation. It indicates success or the reason for failure.

RetCodes appear only in trading methods because only trading operations go through the broker and can be rejected (insufficient margin, invalid price, market closed, etc.).

docs.title: Quick Example: proper RetCode handling
docs.text:
var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);

// ✅ ALWAYS check ReturnedCode explicitly
if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009) // TRADE_RETCODE_DONE
    Console.WriteLine($"✓ Trade successful! Order #{result.Order}");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"✗ Trade failed: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");

Key point: no exception = the API call worked, but you still check ReturnedCode to know whether the trade succeeded.

docs.title: RetCode Source
docs.text:
RetCodes are standard MQL5 codes defined in official MetaQuotes documentation:

MQL5 Documentation: Trade Server Return Codes (ENUM_TRADE_RETCODE)

These codes are:

  • Unified across all languages (C#, Python, Java, Node.js, Go, PHP)
  • Unified with the MT5 terminal — returned directly from the trading server
  • Defined in protobuf — delivered as the uint field ReturnedCode in trading result messages
  • Paired with text — the reply also carries ReturnedCodeDescription, a ready-made human-readable message (no helper lookup needed)

docs.title: 📥 Where is RetCode used in the API?
docs.text: RetCode is returned by all trading operations that modify positions or orders:

docs.title: 1. OrderSend (opening orders)
docs.text:
using mt5_term_api;

var request = new OrderSendRequest
{
    Symbol    = "EURUSD",
    Operation = TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE.Tmt5OrderTypeBuy,
    Volume    = 0.01,
    Price     = await service.GetAskAsync("EURUSD")
};

var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Order opened! Ticket: {result.Order}");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Order failed: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription}");

docs.title: 2. OrderModify (modifying SL/TP)
docs.text:
var result = await service.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, sl: 1.0850, tp: 1.0950);
if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    Console.WriteLine("[OK] SL/TP modified");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Modification failed: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription}");

docs.title: 3. OrderClose (closing positions)
docs.text:
var result = await service.CloseByTicket(ticket);
if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    Console.WriteLine("[OK] Position closed");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Close failed: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription}");

Exceptions vs codes. Depending on the server, a rejected trade may instead surface as an ApiExceptionMT5. That exception exposes the same trade code via ex.MqlErrorTradeIntCode and ex.MqlErrorTradeDescription. Handle both paths (see Error handling).

docs.title: 👁️ Why RetCode only in trading methods?
docs.text:
Informational methods (prices, symbols, balance) do not return a RetCode because:

  • They don't go through the broker.
  • They can't be "rejected" — either the data exists or there's a gRPC error.
  • They read local terminal data.

Trading methods return a RetCode because:

  • The request is sent to the broker via the trading server.
  • The broker validates margin, symbol rules, trading hours, limits.
  • The broker can reject for dozens of reasons — each with a unique code.

docs.title: Complete RetCode List
docs.text: The MQL5 Name column is the official ENUM_TRADE_RETCODE identifier (language-neutral). C# returns the raw uint; if you prefer named constants, see Defining constants in C#.

docs.title: Success Codes
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description When Returned 10009 TRADE_RETCODE_DONE Request completed successfully Market order opened/closed 10010 TRADE_RETCODE_DONE_PARTIAL Partial execution Only part of volume executed 10008 TRADE_RETCODE_PLACED Pending order placed Limit/Stop order placed

docs.title: Requote Codes (retry recommended)
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Action 10004 TRADE_RETCODE_REQUOTE Requote Price changed, retry request 10020 TRADE_RETCODE_PRICE_CHANGED Price changed Similar to requote, retry

docs.title: ⚠️ Request Validation Errors
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Common Cause 10013 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_REQUEST Invalid request Incorrect parameters 10014 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_VOLUME Invalid volume Volume < Min or > Max 10015 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_PRICE Invalid price Price doesn't match symbol rules 10016 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_STOPS Invalid stops SL/TP too close to price (check StopLevel) 10022 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_EXPIRATION Invalid expiration Expiration time incorrect 10030 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_FILL Invalid order filling type Fill type not allowed 10035 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_ORDER Invalid order type Order type prohibited for symbol 10038 TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_CLOSE_VOLUME Invalid close volume Close volume exceeds position volume

docs.title: 🚫 Trading Restrictions
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Reason 10017 TRADE_RETCODE_TRADE_DISABLED Trading disabled Trading disabled for symbol 10018 TRADE_RETCODE_MARKET_CLOSED Market closed Outside trading hours 10026 TRADE_RETCODE_SERVER_DISABLES_AT Autotrading disabled by server Server disabled auto-trading 10027 TRADE_RETCODE_CLIENT_DISABLES_AT Autotrading disabled by client Terminal disabled auto-trading 10032 TRADE_RETCODE_ONLY_REAL Only real accounts Action unavailable on demo 10042 TRADE_RETCODE_LONG_ONLY Only long positions allowed Short positions prohibited 10043 TRADE_RETCODE_SHORT_ONLY Only short positions allowed Long positions prohibited 10044 TRADE_RETCODE_CLOSE_ONLY Only position closing allowed Opening new positions prohibited 10045 TRADE_RETCODE_FIFO_CLOSE Position close only by FIFO rule FIFO rule enforced 10046 TRADE_RETCODE_HEDGE_PROHIBITED Opposite positions prohibited Hedging disabled

docs.title: 💰 Resource Limits
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Solution 10019 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_MONEY Insufficient funds Check free margin 10033 TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_ORDERS Pending orders limit Close some pending orders 10034 TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_VOLUME Volume limit Reduce position volume 10040 TRADE_RETCODE_LIMIT_POSITIONS Positions limit Close some positions

docs.title: 🔄 Technical Issues (Retryable)
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Retryable 10011 TRADE_RETCODE_ERROR Processing error No 10012 TRADE_RETCODE_TIMEOUT Request timeout Yes 10021 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_QUOTES No quotes Yes 10024 TRADE_RETCODE_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Rate limiting Yes (with delay) 10028 TRADE_RETCODE_LOCKED Request locked for processing Yes 10029 TRADE_RETCODE_FROZEN Order or position frozen Yes 10031 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_CONNECTION No connection Yes

docs.title: State Management
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Meaning 10023 TRADE_RETCODE_ORDER_CHANGED Order state changed Order already modified/closed 10025 TRADE_RETCODE_NO_CHANGES No changes New parameters = current parameters 10036 TRADE_RETCODE_POSITION_CLOSED Position closed Position doesn't exist 10039 TRADE_RETCODE_CLOSE_ORDER_EXIST Close order exists Cannot close more than position volume

docs.title: ❌ Rejection Codes
docs.text: Code MQL5 Name Description Reason 10006 TRADE_RETCODE_REJECT Request rejected Broker rejected 10007 TRADE_RETCODE_CANCEL Request canceled Canceled by trader 10041 TRADE_RETCODE_REJECT_CANCEL Pending order activation rejected Activation rejected and canceled

docs.title: Reading the result in C
docs.text:
The SDK does not ship a helper module or named-constant class for RetCodes — you read them directly off the reply:

var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);

Console.WriteLine(result.ReturnedCode);            // e.g. 10018 (uint)
Console.WriteLine(result.ReturnedCodeDescription); // e.g. "Market is closed" (server-provided)

ReturnedCodeDescription already gives you the human-readable text, so there's no get_retcode_message()-style lookup to call.

docs.title: When to explicitly check RetCode
docs.text:
CRITICAL: check ReturnedCode after every trading operation:

// ❌ WRONG — no exception does NOT mean the trade succeeded
var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
Console.WriteLine($"Order placed: {result.Order}"); // Order may be 0 if rejected!

// ✅ CORRECT — always check ReturnedCode
var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    Console.WriteLine($"✓ Order #{result.Order}");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"✗ {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");

Because: no exception means the API call succeeded (connection OK, terminal responded) — it does not mean the trade succeeded. The ReturnedCode is the actual trade result.

docs.title: Defining constants in C
docs.text:
If you dislike magic numbers, drop a small helper into your project:

public static class TradeRetcode
{
    public const uint Done = 10009, DonePartial = 10010, Placed = 10008;
    public const uint Requote = 10004, PriceChanged = 10020;
    public const uint NoMoney = 10019, MarketClosed = 10018, InvalidStops = 10016, InvalidVolume = 10014;

    public static bool IsSuccess(uint c)   => c == Done || c == Placed;
    public static bool IsRequote(uint c)   => c is Requote or PriceChanged;
    public static bool IsRetryable(uint c) => c is 10012 or 10021 or 10024 or 10028 or 10029 or 10031;
}

// Usage
if (TradeRetcode.IsSuccess(result.ReturnedCode)) { /* ... */ }

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
Two independent things can go wrong — handle both:

using Grpc.Core;
using mt5_term_api;

try
{
    var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);

    if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
        Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Order #{result.Order}");
    else
        Console.WriteLine($"[X] Trade rejected: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");
}
catch (ApiExceptionMT5 ex)   // business error surfaced as an exception (carries the trade code)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Trade error: {ex.MqlErrorTradeIntCode} — {ex.MqlErrorTradeDescription}");
}
catch (RpcException ex)      // transport/network error
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] gRPC error: {ex.Status}");
}

docs.title: Example 1 — Basic order placement with RetCode check
docs.text:
using mt5_term_api;
using MetaRPC.CSharpMT5;

var account = new MT5Account(12345678, "your_password", "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync("MetaQuotes-Demo", baseChartSymbol: "EURUSD", timeoutSeconds: 120);

try
{
    var service = new MT5Service(account);

    var request = new OrderSendRequest
    {
        Symbol    = "EURUSD",
        Operation = TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE.Tmt5OrderTypeBuy,
        Volume    = 0.01,
        Price     = await service.GetAskAsync("EURUSD")
    };

    var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
    if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
        Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Order #{result.Order}, volume {result.Volume}, price {result.Price:F5}");
    else
        Console.WriteLine($"[X] {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");
}
finally
{
    await account.DisconnectAsync();
}

docs.title: Example 2 — Handling common errors (switch)
docs.text:
var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);

switch (result.ReturnedCode)
{
    case 10009:
        Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Order #{result.Order}");
        break;
    case 10019: // NO_MONEY
        Console.WriteLine("[WARN] Insufficient funds — reduce volume or add margin");
        break;
    case 10018: // MARKET_CLOSED
        Console.WriteLine("[WARN] Market closed — try during trading hours");
        break;
    case 10016: // INVALID_STOPS
        Console.WriteLine("[WARN] SL/TP too close — increase distance (check StopLevel)");
        break;
    case 10014: // INVALID_VOLUME
        var (min, max, step) = await service.GetVolumeLimitsAsync("EURUSD");
        Console.WriteLine($"[WARN] Invalid volume. Min {min}, Max {max}, Step {step}");
        break;
    case 10004: case 10020: // REQUOTE / PRICE_CHANGED
        Console.WriteLine("[WARN] Price changed — retry");
        break;
    default:
        Console.WriteLine($"[X] {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");
        break;
}

docs.title: Example 3 — Retry logic for transient errors
docs.text:
async Task<OrderSendData> PlaceWithRetryAsync(MT5Service service, OrderSendRequest request, int maxRetries = 3)
{
    for (int attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++)
    {
        var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);

        if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009) return result;                 // success

        if (result.ReturnedCode is 10004 or 10020)                       // requote → retry now
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Requote on attempt {attempt}, retrying...");
            await Task.Delay(100);
            request.Price = await service.GetAskAsync(request.Symbol);   // refresh price
            continue;
        }

        if (result.ReturnedCode is 10012 or 10021 or 10024 or 10028 or 10029 or 10031) // transient
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Transient error on attempt {attempt}, waiting {attempt}s...");
            await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(attempt));             // simple backoff
            continue;
        }

        throw new InvalidOperationException($"Permanent error: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} ({result.ReturnedCode})");
    }
    throw new InvalidOperationException($"Failed after {maxRetries} attempts");
}

docs.title: Example 4 — Modifying SL/TP with validation
docs.text:
var result = await service.ModifySlTpAsync(123456, sl: 1.0850, tp: 1.0950);

switch (result.ReturnedCode)
{
    case 10009: Console.WriteLine("[OK] SL/TP updated"); break;
    case 10025: Console.WriteLine("[WARN] No changes — new SL/TP equals current"); break;      // NO_CHANGES
    case 10036: Console.WriteLine("[WARN] Position already closed"); break;                     // POSITION_CLOSED
    case 10016: Console.WriteLine("[X] Invalid SL/TP distance (check StopLevel)"); break;       // INVALID_STOPS
    default:    Console.WriteLine($"[X] {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} ({result.ReturnedCode})"); break;
}

docs.title: ✅ DO
docs.text:
1. Always check ReturnedCode after trading operations.
  2. Use ReturnedCodeDescription for the message — it's already human-readable.
  3. Retry requotes (10004, 10020) after refreshing the price.
  4. Check margin before trading to avoid 10019: 
    double freeMargin = await service.GetFreeMarginAsync();
double required   = await service.CalculateBuyMarginAsync("EURUSD", 0.01);
if (freeMargin < required) Console.WriteLine("Insufficient margin!");

docs.title: ❌ DON'T
docs.text:
1. Don't assume no exception = success — check ReturnedCode too.
  2. Don't retry permanent errors (insufficient margin, market closed).
  3. Don't swallow ApiExceptionMT5 / RpcException silently — a rejected trade may arrive as an exception carrying MqlErrorTradeIntCode.
  4. Don't hard-code bare numbers everywhere — centralize them (see Defining constants in C#).

docs.title: ℹ️ Quick Reference Table
docs.text: Category RetCodes Action Success 10008, 10009, 10010 Continue normally Requote 10004, 10020 Retry immediately (refresh price) Temporary 10012, 10021, 10024, 10028, 10029, 10031 Retry with delay Validation 10013–10016, 10022, 10030, 10035, 10038 Fix parameters Restrictions 10017, 10018, 10026, 10027, 10032, 10042–10046 Check trading conditions Limits 10019, 10033, 10034, 10040 Reduce volume/positions State 10023, 10025, 10036, 10039 Check current state Rejection 10006, 10007, 10041 Check request Technical 10011 Contact support
