docs.title: Synchronous vs Asynchronous Methods - When to Use What (C#)
docs.text: Understanding execution models in CSharpMT5: non-blocking streaming vs synchronous execution.

docs.title: 🎯 Quick Comparison
docs.text:
All I/O, gRPC queries, and streaming in C# use async/await with Task and IAsyncEnumerable<T>. Synchronous variants exist for legacy desktop scenarios.

Aspect Asynchronous Pattern Synchronous Call Thread Blocking ❌ Non-blocking (high concurrency) ✅ Blocks current thread Throughput ✅ Handles thousands of events/sec ❌ Limited by thread pool Real-Time Data ✅ Perfect for tick & trade streams ⚠️ Inefficient for streams Simplicity Requires async runtime awareness Simple, linear execution Recommended for Automated bots, microservices, GUIs CLI scripts, notebooks, one-offs

docs.title: 1. Market Data Streaming
docs.text:
Market ticks arrive at microsecond intervals during peak sessions. Streaming methods return IAsyncEnumerable<T>; consume them with await foreach so your thread is never blocked while waiting for the next tick:

var account = new MT5Account(user, password, "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync("YourBroker-Demo", baseChartSymbol: "EURUSD");

using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
try
{
    await foreach (var tickData in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(new[] { "EURUSD" }, cts.Token))
        Console.WriteLine($"Bid={tickData.SymbolTick.Bid:F5}, Ask={tickData.SymbolTick.Ask:F5}");
}
catch (OperationCanceledException) { /* stopped after timeout */ }

await account.DisconnectAsync();

See the gRPC Streaming guide for full subscription patterns.

docs.title: 2. High-Frequency Order Execution
docs.text:
When operating across multiple currency pairs simultaneously, asynchronous dispatch lets your bot fan out requests concurrently instead of sequentially:

// Query several symbols at once instead of one-by-one
var ticks = await Task.WhenAll(
    new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY" }.Select(s => account.SymbolInfoTickAsync(s)));

foreach (var t in ticks)
    Console.WriteLine($"{t.Bid:F5} / {t.Ask:F5}");

docs.title: 🐢 When to Use Synchronous Methods
docs.text:
Every async method has a blocking twin — drop the Async suffix: AccountSummary(), SymbolInfoTick("EURUSD"), OrderSend(request), ConnectByServerName(...), Disconnect(). Each simply calls the async version and waits, which is convenient for linear scripts, REPL/notebook exploration, or small one-off CLI tools where concurrency doesn't matter.

var account = new MT5Account(user, password, "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443", apiKey);
account.ConnectByServerName("YourBroker-Demo", "EURUSD");   // blocks until connected

var summary = account.AccountSummary();                     // blocks until the reply arrives
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance} {summary.AccountCurrency}");

account.Disconnect();

Caution: don't call a synchronous method on a UI thread or from inside an async context — blocking on a Task there can deadlock and defeats the concurrency async buys you. In those cases always await the async variant. Streaming has no synchronous form — subscriptions are always consumed with await foreach.

docs.title: 💡 Summary
docs.text: Always prefer asynchronous paradigms for production bots, multi-symbol trading, and background services. Use synchronous wrappers for quick setup scripts, testing, or exploratory analysis.

docs.title: What is this?
docs.text:
This is your sandbox for writing custom MT5 trading code in C#. Connection setup is already done — you only add your trading logic inside RunAsync().

File: Examples/UserCode/ProgramUserCode.cs

docs.title: 🏁 Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Enable the command — uncomment the usercode case block in Program.cs (around line ~172).
  2. Open Examples/UserCode/ProgramUserCode.cs — write your code, or uncomment the ready examples.
  3. Run: 
    dotnet run usercode

That's it — your code runs with a live MT5 connection (and disconnects cleanly in finally).

docs.title: Option 1 — Uncomment examples
docs.text:
ProgramUserCode.cs ships with ready-to-use examples. Just remove the //:

// Example 1: Get account information
// var summary = await service.AccountSummaryAsync();
// Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance} {summary.AccountCurrency}");

docs.title: Available commands
docs.text:
dotnet run usercode
dotnet run user
dotnet run sandbox

docs.title: What's already configured
docs.text:
• Connection — MT5 terminal connected via gRPC (ConnectionHelper.CreateAndConnectAccountAsync)
  • Configuration — loaded from Config/appsettings.json
  • account — low-level gRPC client (MT5Account)
  • service — mid-level wrapper (MT5Service); the high-level Sugar helpers are extension methods on it, so you call them as service.PlaceMarket(...), service.BuyMarketByRisk(...), etc.
  • async/await — all methods are asynchronous (each also has a blocking sync twin)

There is no separate sugar variable: MT5Sugar is a set of extension methods on MT5Service, so everything hangs off service.

docs.title: 🧩 Can I mix API levels?
docs.text:
Yes — all three layers are reachable from the two variables:

// Low-level (direct gRPC): rich protobuf object
MT5Account acc = account;
AccountSummaryData summary = await acc.AccountSummaryAsync();
double balanceLow = summary.AccountBalance;

// Mid-level (MT5Service): unwrapped primitive
double balanceSvc = await service.GetBalanceAsync();

// High-level (Sugar extension on service)
var result = await service.BuyMarketByRisk("EURUSD", stopPoints: 20, riskMoney: 10.0);
  • account — full control (gRPC protobuf)
  • service — convenient wrappers and Sugar helpers

docs.title: Get account information
docs.text:
// Mid-level shortcuts (easiest)
double balance = await service.GetBalanceAsync();
double equity  = await service.GetEquityAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {balance:F2} | Equity: {equity:F2}");

// Full snapshot (one call)
var summary = await service.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance:F2} {summary.AccountCurrency}");

docs.title: Get current price
docs.text:
double bid = await service.GetBidAsync("EURUSD");
double ask = await service.GetAskAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD: Bid={bid:F5}, Ask={ask:F5}");

// Or the full tick
var tick = await service.SymbolInfoTickAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"Bid={tick.Bid:F5}, Ask={tick.Ask:F5}");

docs.title: Open a market order
docs.text:
// Simple market BUY
var r1 = await service.BuyMarketAsync("EURUSD", 0.01);

// Generic market order (BUY/SELL) with optional SL/TP
var r2 = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", 0.01, isBuy: true, sl: 1.0800, tp: 1.0900);

// Risk-based sizing: 20-point stop, risk $10
var r3 = await service.BuyMarketByRisk("EURUSD", stopPoints: 20, riskMoney: 10.0, tpPoints: 40);

if (r3.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    Console.WriteLine($"✅ Order #{r3.Order}, volume {r3.Volume}, price {r3.Price:F5}");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ {r3.ReturnedCodeDescription}");

docs.title: Place a pending order (points-based)
docs.text:
// Buy Limit 50 points below Ask, SL 100 / TP 200 points
await service.BuyLimitPoints("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: 50, slPoints: 100, tpPoints: 200);

// Sell Stop 50 points below Bid
await service.SellStopPoints("EURUSD", 0.01, priceOffsetPoints: 50, slPoints: 100, tpPoints: 200);

docs.title: Get open positions
docs.text:
var opened = await service.OpenedOrdersAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Open positions: {opened.PositionInfos.Count}");
foreach (var pos in opened.PositionInfos)
    Console.WriteLine($"  #{pos.Ticket} {pos.Symbol} {pos.Volume:F2} lot, Profit: {pos.Profit:F2}");

docs.title: Close positions
docs.text:
await service.CloseByTicket(ticket);          // specific position
await service.CloseAllPositions("EURUSD");     // all market positions for a symbol
await service.CloseAllPositions();             // all positions (all symbols)
await service.CancelAll("EURUSD");             // cancel pending orders for a symbol

docs.title: Modify a position
docs.text: await service.ModifySlTpAsync(ticket, sl: 1.0850, tp: 1.0950);

docs.title: Calculate position size by risk
docs.text:
double volume = await service.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 200, riskMoney: 10.0);
Console.WriteLine($"Volume for $10 risk with 200-point SL: {volume:F2} lot");
var result = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", volume, isBuy: true);

docs.title: Return Codes (RetCodes)
docs.text:
Always check ReturnedCode after trading operations!

using mt5_term_api;

var request = new OrderSendRequest
{
    Symbol    = "EURUSD",
    Operation = TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE.Tmt5OrderTypeBuy,
    Volume    = 0.01,
    Price     = (await service.GetAskAsync("EURUSD"))  // market BUY uses current Ask
};

var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);

if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)       // market order executed
    Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Order #{result.Order}");
else if (result.ReturnedCode == 10008)  // pending order placed
    Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Pending order #{result.Order}");
else
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Failed: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");

Common RetCodes:

  • 10009 — market order executed successfully
  • 10008 — pending order placed successfully
  • 10019 — not enough money (insufficient margin)
  • 10016 — invalid stops (SL/TP too close to price)
  • 10018 — market closed

Full list: RETURN_CODES_REFERENCE.md

docs.title: ℹ️ Error handling
docs.text: Two independent things can go wrong — handle both:

docs.title: 1. Connection / network errors → exceptions
docs.text:
using Grpc.Core;

try
{
    var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
}
catch (ApiExceptionMT5 ex)   // business error from the server
{
    Console.WriteLine($"API error: {ex.ErrorCode}");
}
catch (RpcException ex)       // transport/network error
{
    Console.WriteLine($"gRPC error: {ex.Status}");
}

docs.title: 2. Trade rejections → ReturnedCode
docs.text:
var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
if (result.ReturnedCode != 10009)
    Console.WriteLine($"Trade rejected: {result.ReturnedCodeDescription}");

docs.title: Recommended pattern
docs.text:
try
{
    var result = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
    if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
        Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Order #{result.Order}");
    else
        Console.WriteLine($"[X] {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");
}
catch (Exception ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Error: {ex.Message}");
}

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
1. Start simple — uncomment one example at a time.
  2. Use Sugar helpers — BuyMarketByRisk(...) and CalcVolumeForRiskAsync(...) are easier than hand-building requests.
  3. Check ReturnedCode — always validate trading operations (10009 = success).
  4. Test on demo — make sure you're on a demo account first.
  5. Read the return codes — RETURN_CODES_REFERENCE.md explains every code.
  6. Use async/await — every method is async; don't forget await.
  7. IDE autocomplete — the strongly-typed API surfaces everything as you type.
  8. Browse examples — see the Examples/ folder (LowLevel, Service, Sugar, Orchestrators).

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
❌ Forgot await 

var balance = service.GetBalanceAsync(); // returns a Task, not the value!

✅ Always await 

var balance = await service.GetBalanceAsync();

❌ Not handling exceptions 

var r = await service.OrderSendAsync(request); // may throw on network/API error

✅ Wrap in try/catch 

try { var r = await service.OrderSendAsync(request); }
catch (Exception ex) { Console.WriteLine($"Error: {ex.Message}"); }

❌ Not checking ReturnedCode 

var r = await service.OrderSendAsync(request); // assuming success!

✅ Check it 

var r = await service.OrderSendAsync(request);
if (r.ReturnedCode != 10009) { Console.WriteLine($"Failed: {r.ReturnedCodeDescription}"); return; }

docs.title: Example: complete sandbox body
docs.text:
A minimal strategy with proper error handling (the connection scaffolding is already provided by ProgramUserCode.RunAsync):

// account (MT5Account) and service (MT5Service) are already connected.

// 1) Account state
double balance = await service.GetBalanceAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {balance:F2}");

// 2) Size by risk: $ (1% of balance), 50-point stop
double risk   = balance * 0.01;
double volume = await service.CalcVolumeForRiskAsync("EURUSD", stopPoints: 50, riskMoney: risk);

// 3) Open and validate
try
{
    var result = await service.PlaceMarket("EURUSD", volume, isBuy: true);
    if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
        Console.WriteLine($"[OK] Position #{result.Order} with {volume:F2} lot");
    else
        Console.WriteLine($"[X] {result.ReturnedCodeDescription} (code {result.ReturnedCode})");
}
catch (Exception ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[X] Error: {ex.Message}");
}

Happy trading!

docs.title: Your First Project in 10 Minutes (C#)
docs.text: Hands-on Quick Start - Create a working trading project with MetaTrader 5 and CSharpMT5 from scratch.

docs.title: Step 0: Obtain Your API Key
docs.text:
To connect to MetaRPC endpoints (mt5.mrpc.pro:443), obtain your API key:

  1. Register for free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.

  2. Generate your API token in your dashboard at https://mrpc.pro/my.

  3. Set your token in your environment or connection config.

docs.title: Step 1: Create Your Project
docs.text:
Create a new directory for your trading bot:

mkdir my_csharpmt5_bot
cd my_csharpmt5_bot

Install the package:

dotnet add package MetaRPC.MT5

docs.title: Step 2: Write Your Trading Code
docs.text:
Create your main application file and paste the following snippet:

using mt5_term_api;
using MetaRPC.CSharpMT5;

// user / password / serverName from your MT5 demo account;
// grpcServer e.g. "https://mt5.mrpc.pro:443"; apiKey your MetaRPC key (or null for env/TRIAL).
// Session ID generation on Connect and authentication are handled automatically.
var account = new MT5Account(user, password, grpcServer, apiKey);
await account.ConnectByServerNameAsync(serverName, baseChartSymbol: "EURUSD", timeoutSeconds: 30);

var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: {summary.AccountBalance}, Equity: {summary.AccountEquity}");

await account.DisconnectAsync();

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Program
docs.text:
Run your application:

dotnet run

Expected output:

Balance: 10000.00, Equity: 10000.00

docs.text:

  • Explore gRPC Streaming to listen to live ticks.

  • Learn about high-level risk management and convenience helpers in MT5Sugar.

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (gRPC protocol)
docs.text: Every method is available in two versions: Async (recommended) and Sync (rare scenarios).

docs.title: Async Version (Recommended - 99% of cases)
docs.text:
var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
var tick = await account.SymbolInfoTickAsync("EURUSD");

docs.title: Sync Version (Legacy/specific scenarios only)
docs.text:
var summary = account.AccountSummary();
var tick = account.SymbolInfoTick("EURUSD");

📖 Read: Sync vs Async - When to Use What - Detailed guide with use cases and performance comparisons.

Every method follows the same shape:

  • Proto Service/Method: Service.Method(Request) → Reply
  • C# wrapper: await mt5Account.MethodAsync(...) or mt5Account.Method()
  • Reply structure: Reply.Data payload (proto-generated objects)
  • Return codes: 10009 = success; other codes = check error message

Timestamps = UTC (google.protobuf.Timestamp). For streaming subscriptions, use IAsyncEnumerable<T> with await foreach pattern.

docs.title: Layer 1: MT5Account (Low-Level)
docs.text:
What: Direct proto/gRPC communication with MT5 terminal.

When to use: - Need full control over protocol - Building custom wrappers - Proto-level integration required

Characteristics: - Works with proto Request/Response objects - Raw gRPC method calls - Complete access to all MT5 functions - Highest complexity

Location: package/Helpers/MT5Account.cs (NuGet package source)

Documentation: This folder (you are here!)

docs.title: Layer 2: MT5Service
docs.text:
What: Simplified wrapper methods without proto complexity.

When to use: - Want simplified API but not auto-normalization - Building custom convenience layers - Need direct data returns

Characteristics: - Simple method signatures - Type conversions (proto → C# primitives) - No proto objects in return values - No auto-normalization

Location: MT5Service.cs

Documentation: MT5Service.Overview.md

docs.title: Layer 3: MT5Sugar
docs.text:
What: High-level convenience API with ~50 smart methods.

When to use: - Most trading scenarios (95% of cases) - Want auto-normalization - Need risk management helpers - Building strategies quickly

Characteristics: - Auto-normalization of volumes/prices - Risk-based position sizing - Batch operations - Smart helpers

Location: MT5Sugar.cs

Documentation: MT5Sugar.API_Overview.md

docs.title: 🎓 Learning Path
docs.text: Recommended sequence: Start from foundation (MT5Account) → Build up to convenience layers (MT5Service → MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Step 1: Master the Foundation (MT5Account)
docs.text:
Why first: MT5Account is the foundation - everything else is built on top of it. Understanding the protocol level gives you complete control.

1. Read: This documentation folder (docs/MT5Account/)
2. Study: Proto definitions and gRPC communication
3. Understand: Request/Response patterns
4. Learn: Return codes and error handling

Why second: Once you know the foundation, see how MT5Service simplifies it by wrapping proto objects.

1. Study: How MT5Service wraps MT5Account methods
2. Compare: Wrapper vs low-level implementations

docs.title: Proto Return Codes
docs.text:
• 10009 = Success / DONE
  • 10004 = Requote
  • 10006 = Request rejected
  • 10013 = Invalid request
  • 10014 = Invalid volume
  • 10015 = Invalid price
  • 10016 = Invalid stops
  • 10018 = Market closed
  • 10019 = Not enough money
  • 10031 = No connection with trade server

Always check ReturnedCode field in trading operations.

Complete Reference: Return Codes Reference

docs.title: C# Async Patterns
docs.text:
Request/Reply methods: 

var result = await account.MethodAsync(parameters, deadline, cancellationToken);

Streaming methods: 

await foreach (var data in account.OnMethodAsync(parameters, cancellationToken))
{
    // Process streaming data
}

Detailed Guide: Sync_vs_Async.md - When to use async vs sync, performance comparisons, best practices

docs.title: ⚠️ Important Notes
docs.text:
• Demo account first: Always test on demo before live trading.
  • Check return codes: Every trading operation returns status code.
  • Validate parameters: Use OrderCheckAsync() before OrderSendAsync().
  • Handle errors: Network/protocol errors can occur.
  • Thread safety: Streams execute on background threads.
  • Resource cleanup: Unsubscribe from streams when done (use CancellationToken).
  • UTC timestamps: All times are in UTC, not local time.
  • Broker limitations: Not all brokers support all features (DOM, hedging, etc.).
  • Async/await: Always use await with async methods.
  • CancellationToken: Always provide cancellation tokens for long-running operations.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
try
{
    var result = await account.OrderSendAsync(request);
    if (result.ReturnedCode == 10009)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("✅ Success");
    }
    else
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"❌ Error: {result.Comment}");
    }
}
catch (RpcException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"gRPC Error: {ex.Status}");
}

docs.title: Streaming with Cancellation
docs.text:
var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5));
try
{
    await foreach (var tick in account.OnSymbolTickAsync(symbols, cts.Token))
    {
        // Process tick
    }
}
catch (OperationCanceledException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Stream stopped");
}

"Trade safe, code clean, and may your async operations always complete successfully."

docs.title: ✅ Getting Individual Account Double Properties
docs.text:
Request: single double property from MT5 account. Fetch specific numeric properties like balance, equity, margin, profit, etc.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT5Account.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT5)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Proto definition: AccountInfoDouble (defined in mt5-term-api-account-information.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • Method: AccountInfoDouble(AccountInfoDoubleRequest) → AccountInfoDoubleReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): AccountInformation.AccountInfoDouble(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace MetaRPC.CSharpMT5
{
    public class MT5Account
    {
        public async Task<double> AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
            AccountInfoDoublePropertyType property,
            DateTime? deadline = null,
            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

AccountInfoDoubleRequest { property_id: AccountInfoDoublePropertyType }

Reply message:

AccountInfoDoubleReply { data: AccountInfoDoubleData } or { error: Error }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description property AccountInfoDoublePropertyType ✅ Property to retrieve (see enum below) deadline DateTime? ❌ Absolute per‑call UTC deadline → converted to timeout cancellationToken CancellationToken ❌ Cooperative cancel for the call/retry loop

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoDoubleData
docs.text:
Field Type Description RequestedValue double The requested property value

The method returns double directly (unwrapped from the proto message).

docs.title: AccountInfoDoublePropertyType
docs.text: Enum Value Value Description MQL5 Docs AccountBalance 0 Account balance in the deposit currency AccountInfoDouble AccountCredit 1 Account credit in the deposit currency AccountProfit 2 Current profit of an account in the deposit currency AccountEquity 3 Account equity in the deposit currency (Balance + Profit) AccountMargin 4 Account margin used in the deposit currency AccountMarginFree 5 Free margin of an account in the deposit currency AccountMarginLevel 6 Account margin level in percents AccountMarginSoCall 7 Margin call level. Depending on the set AccountMarginSoMode is expressed in percents or in the deposit currency AccountMarginSoSo 8 Margin stop out level. Depending on the set AccountMarginSoMode is expressed in percents or in the deposit currency AccountMarginInitial 9 Initial margin. The amount reserved on an account to cover the margin of all pending orders AccountMarginMaintenance 10 Maintenance margin. The minimum equity reserved on an account to cover the minimum amount of all open positions AccountAssets 11 The current assets of an account AccountLiabilities 12 The current liabilities on an account AccountCommissionBlocked 13 The current blocked commission amount on an account

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning one specific double property of the account.
  • Why you need it. When you only need one property (e.g., margin level before placing an order) instead of fetching the full account summary.
  • Performance. Lightweight call — ideal for frequent checks of specific properties.
  • Alternative. Use AccountSummaryAsync() if you need multiple properties at once.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Check a single account property (margin, equity, profit, etc.) without fetching all account data.
  • Monitor specific properties frequently (e.g., margin level for risk management).
  • Verify free margin before placing trades.
  • Calculate margin requirements dynamically.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prefer AccountSummaryAsync() if you need multiple properties — it's more efficient to fetch all data in one call.
  • Use short per‑call timeout (3–5s) with retries for margin checks before trading operations.
  • All MT5Account methods have built-in protection against transient gRPC errors with automatic reconnection.
  • For UI dashboards displaying multiple properties, use AccountSummaryAsync() instead.
  • The method returns double directly (not wrapped in a proto message) for convenience.

docs.title: 1) Check margin level before placing order
docs.text:
// Ensure sufficient margin before trading
var marginLevel = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountMarginLevel,
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));

if (marginLevel < 200.0)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ Warning: Low margin level {marginLevel:F2}%");
    // Skip trading or reduce position size
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"✅ Margin level OK: {marginLevel:F2}%");
}

docs.title: 2) Get current profit
docs.text:
// Monitor floating profit/loss
var profit = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountProfit);
Console.WriteLine($"Current P/L: {profit:F2}");

docs.title: 3) Check free margin
docs.text:
// Verify free margin before opening position
var freeMargin = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountMarginFree);

Console.WriteLine($"Free margin: {freeMargin:F2}");

if (freeMargin < 100.0)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ Insufficient free margin");
}

docs.title: 4) Monitor margin usage
docs.text:
// Fetch margin-related properties
var margin = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountMargin);
var marginFree = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountMarginFree);
var marginLevel = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountMarginLevel);

Console.WriteLine($"Margin:       {margin:F2}");
Console.WriteLine($"Free:         {marginFree:F2}");
Console.WriteLine($"Level:        {marginLevel:F2}%");

docs.title: 5) Compare equity vs balance
docs.text:
// Calculate floating P/L by comparing equity and balance
var balance = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance);
var equity = await acct.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountEquity);

var floatingPL = equity - balance;
Console.WriteLine($"Balance:      {balance:F2}");
Console.WriteLine($"Equity:       {equity:F2}");
Console.WriteLine($"Floating P/L: {floatingPL:F2}");

docs.title: AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType
docs.text: Enum Value Value Description MQL5 Docs AccountLogin 0 Account number AccountInfoInteger AccountTradeMode 1 Account trade mode (Demo/Contest/Real) — see MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode AccountLeverage 2 Account leverage (e.g., 100 for 1:100) AccountLimitOrders 3 Maximum allowed number of open positions and active pending orders (in total). 0 = unlimited AccountMarginSoMode 4 Mode for setting the minimal allowed margin — see EnumAccountStopOutMode (not yet documented) AccountTradeAllowed 5 Allowed trade for the current account (returns 1 or 0) AccountTradeExpert 6 Allowed trade for an Expert Advisor (returns 1 or 0) AccountMarginMode 7 Margin calculation mode — see EnumAccountMarginMode (not yet documented) AccountCurrencyDigits 8 The number of decimal places in the account currency, which are required for an accurate display of trading results AccountFifoClose 9 An indication showing that positions can only be closed by FIFO rule.   • MrpcAccountTradeModeContest = 1 — contest

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning one specific long property of the account.
  • Why you need it. When you only need one integer property (e.g., leverage, login, trade mode) instead of fetching the full account summary.
  • Performance. Lightweight call — ideal for quick checks of specific properties.
  • Type note. All properties return long (int64), even boolean flags (1 = true, 0 = false).
  • Alternative. Use AccountSummaryAsync() if you need multiple properties at once.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Check a single integer account property without fetching all account data.
  • Verify account leverage before calculating position sizes.
  • Check if trading is allowed (AccountTradeAllowed, AccountTradeExpert).
  • Determine account trade mode (demo/contest/real).
  • Check position limits (AccountLimitOrders).
  • Verify FIFO close rules or hedging permissions.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prefer AccountSummaryAsync() if you need multiple properties — it's more efficient to fetch all data in one call.
  • Boolean properties return 1 (true) or 0 (false) as long values.
  • Use short per‑call timeout (3–5s) with retries when checking permissions before trading operations.
  • All MT5Account methods have built-in protection against transient gRPC errors with automatic reconnection.
  • The method returns long directly (not wrapped in a proto message) for convenience.

docs.title: 1) Get account login
docs.text:
// Retrieve account login number
var login = await acct.AccountInfoIntegerAsync(
    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountLogin,
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));
Console.WriteLine($"Account login: {login}");

docs.title: 2) Check account leverage
docs.text:
// Get current leverage setting
var leverage = await acct.AccountInfoIntegerAsync(
    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountLeverage);
Console.WriteLine($"Account leverage: 1:{leverage}");

docs.title: 3) Verify trading is allowed
docs.text:
// Check if trading is enabled for this account
var tradeAllowed = await acct.AccountInfoIntegerAsync(
    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountTradeAllowed);

if (tradeAllowed == 0)
{

    return;
}

// Check if EA trading is allowed
var expertAllowed = await acct.AccountInfoIntegerAsync(
    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountTradeExpert);

if (expertAllowed == 0)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ Expert Advisor trading is disabled");
}

docs.text:
// Determine if account is demo, contest, or real
var tradeMode = await acct.AccountInfoIntegerAsync(
    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountTradeMode);

var modeLabel = tradeMode switch
{
    0 => "Demo",
    1 => "Contest",
    2 => "Real",

    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountLimitOrders);

{

}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ Max positions + pending orders: {limitOrders}");
}

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning one specific string property of the account.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Get the account currency for display or calculations.
  • Retrieve the broker/company name for logging or verification.
  • Fetch the client name for personalized UI.
  • Get the server name for diagnostics or multi-account management.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Prefer AccountSummaryAsync() if you need multiple properties — it's more efficient to fetch all data in one call.

  • Use short per‑call timeout (3–5s) with retries when fetching properties for UI display.
  • All MT5Account methods have built-in protection against transient gRPC errors with automatic reconnection.
  • The method returns string directly (not wrapped in a proto message) for convenience.

• What it is. Single RPC returning account state: balance, equity, currency, leverage, trade mode, server time.
  • Why you need it. Fast dashboard/CLI status; double‑check login/currency/leverage; heartbeat via ServerTime.
  • Sanity check. If you see AccountLogin, AccountCurrency, AccountLeverage, AccountEquity → connection is alive.

Use it to display real‑time account state and sanity‑check connectivity:

docs.title: 1) Per‑call deadline
docs.text:
// Enforce a short absolute UTC deadline to avoid hanging calls
var summary = await acct.AccountSummaryAsync(
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));
Console.WriteLine($"[deadline] Equity={summary.AccountEquity:F2}");

docs.title: 2) Cooperative cancellation (with CancellationToken)

// Allow a graceful stop from another task
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
cts.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3));
var s2 = await acct.AccountSummaryAsync(
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3),
    cancellationToken: cts.Token);
Console.WriteLine($"[cancel] Currency={s2.AccountCurrency}");

docs.text:
var s = await acct.AccountSummaryAsync();

             $"Bal {s.AccountBalance:F2} | Eq {s.AccountEquity:F2} | " +
             $"Lev {s.AccountLeverage} | Mode {s.AccountTradeMode}";

docs.title: 4) Human‑readable server time with timezone shift
docs.text:
var x = await acct.AccountSummaryAsync();
var serverUtc = x.ServerTime.ToDateTime(); // generated Timestamp → DateTime
var shift = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(x.UtcTimezoneServerTimeShiftMinutes);
var serverLocal = serverUtc + shift;
Console.WriteLine($"Server time: {serverLocal:O} (shift {shift})");

docs.title: 5) Map proto → thin view‑model
docs.text:
// Keep only what UI needs; fast and test‑friendly
public record AccountSummaryView(
    long Login,
    string Currency,
    double Balance,
    double Equity,
    long Leverage,
    int Mode)
{
    public static AccountSummaryView FromProto(AccountSummaryData p) =>
        new(
            Login: p.AccountLogin,
            Currency: p.AccountCurrency,
            Balance: p.AccountBalance,
            Equity: p.AccountEquity,
            Leverage: p.AccountLeverage,
            Mode: (int)p.AccountTradeMode
        );
}

var proto = await acct.AccountSummaryAsync();
var view = AccountSummaryView.FromProto(proto);
Console.WriteLine(view);

docs.title: MT5Account · Account Information - Overview
docs.text: Account balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, and other account properties. Use this page to choose the right API for accessing account state.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• AccountSummary - all account info at once (balance, equity, margin, leverage, profit, etc.).
  • AccountInfoDouble - single double value from account (balance, equity, margin, profit, credit, etc.).
  • AccountInfoInteger - single integer value from account (login, leverage, limit orders, etc.).
  • AccountInfoString - single string value from account (name, server, currency, company).

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• AccountSummary → the one-stop shop for complete account snapshot (balance, equity, margin level, etc.).
  • AccountInfoDouble → grab one numeric property when you need just balance or margin.
  • AccountInfoInteger → grab one integer property like login number or leverage.
  • AccountInfoString → grab one text property like account name or currency.

Rule of thumb: need full snapshot → AccountSummaryAsync; need one specific value → AccountInfo*Async (Double/Integer/String).

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Key inputs Complete account snapshot (all values) AccountSummaryAsync Full account data object (none) One numeric value (balance, equity, margin, etc.) AccountInfoDoubleAsync Single double Property enum (BALANCE, EQUITY, etc.) One integer value (login, leverage, etc.) AccountInfoIntegerAsync Single long Property enum (LOGIN, LEVERAGE, etc.) One text value (name, currency, server, etc.) AccountInfoStringAsync Single string Property enum (NAME, CURRENCY, etc.)

docs.title: ❌ Cross‑refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Margin Level = (Equity / Margin) × 100 - watch for stop-out level.
  • Free Margin = Equity - Margin - available for new positions.
  • AccountSummary includes everything; use it for dashboards.
  • AccountInfo* methods are lighter if you only need one property.
  • Currency affects how profits are calculated - always check account currency.
  • Leverage determines margin requirements - higher leverage = less margin needed.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Get complete account snapshot
var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: ${summary.AccountBalance:F2}, Equity: ${summary.AccountEquity:F2}, Leverage: 1:{summary.AccountLeverage}");

// Get single property - account balance
var balance = await account.AccountInfoDoubleAsync(
    AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.AccountBalance
);
Console.WriteLine($"Balance: ${balance:F2}");

// Get account leverage
var leverage = await account.AccountInfoIntegerAsync(
    AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.AccountLeverage
);
Console.WriteLine($"Leverage: 1:{leverage}");

// Get account currency
var currency = await account.AccountInfoStringAsync(
    AccountInfoStringPropertyType.AccountCurrency
);
Console.WriteLine($"Currency: {currency}");

// Check account balance and equity
var summary = await account.AccountSummaryAsync();
var balance = summary.AccountBalance;
var equity = summary.AccountEquity;
if (equity < balance * 0.8)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ Warning: Equity below 80% of balance!");
}

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Streaming: SubscribeToPositionProfit - real-time equity/profit updates
  • Trading calculations: OrderCalcMargin - calculate required margin before trading
  • Positions: PositionsTotal - count open positions

docs.title: ✅ Historical Price Bars (PriceHistoryAsync)
docs.text:
Request: Get historical OHLC bars for a symbol and timeframe over a time window on MT5.

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT5Account.PriceHistoryAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT5)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: PriceHistory (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: PriceHistory(PriceHistoryRequest) → PriceHistoryReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): MarketInfo.MarketInfoClient.PriceHistory(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace MetaRPC.CSharpMT5
{
    public class MT5Account
    {
        public async Task<PriceHistoryData> PriceHistoryAsync(
            PriceHistoryRequest request,
            DateTime? deadline = null,
            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

PriceHistoryRequest { symbol, timeframe, from_time, to_time }

Reply message:

PriceHistoryReply { data: PriceHistoryData }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description request PriceHistoryRequest Protobuf request with symbol, timeframe and time range deadline DateTime? Absolute per‑call UTC deadline → converted to timeout cancellationToken CancellationToken Cooperative cancel for the call/retry loop

docs.title: PriceHistoryRequest
docs.text: Field Type Description Symbol string Trading symbol Timeframe int Raw MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES value (see table below) FromTime long Window start, Unix seconds. Leave From/To at 0 for newest bars ToTime long Window end, Unix seconds

docs.title: Common Timeframe values (MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES)
docs.text: Timeframe Value PERIOD_M1 1 PERIOD_M5 5 PERIOD_M15 15 PERIOD_M30 30 PERIOD_H1 16385 PERIOD_H4 16388 PERIOD_D1 16408 PERIOD_W1 32769 PERIOD_MN1 49153

docs.text: Field Type Description Bars repeated PriceBar OHLC bars in the window

docs.title: PriceBar
docs.text: Field Type Description Time long Bar open time (Unix seconds) Open double Open price High double High price Low double Low price Close double Close price TickVolume long Tick volume Spread int Spread in points RealVolume long Real (exchange) volume, if provided

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. OHLC candles for a symbol over a time window.
  • Why you need it. Indicators, backtests, charts — anything needing bar history.
  • Timeframe is raw: Pass the MQL5 enum value (H1 = 16385), not minutes.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to pull candles for analysis:

  • Compute indicators (MA, RSI) over recent bars.
  • Seed a chart or a backtest window.
  • Detect ranges/breakouts from the last N bars.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Unix seconds: Convert with DateTimeOffset.ToUnixTimeSeconds(); read back with DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(bar.Time).
  • Newest bars shortcut: Leaving FromTime/ToTime at 0 returns the newest bars — handy for "just give me the latest".
  • Select first: Ensure the symbol is in Market Watch (SymbolSelect) so history is available.
  • Friendly wrapper: MT5Sugar.PriceBarsLast(symbol, "H1", days) accepts a string timeframe and a days window.

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days of H1 bars
docs.text:
// acc — connected MT5Account
var req = new PriceHistoryRequest
{
    Symbol    = "EURUSD",
    Timeframe = 16385, // PERIOD_H1
    FromTime  = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(-7).ToUnixTimeSeconds(),
    ToTime    = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
};

var data = await acc.PriceHistoryAsync(req);
Console.WriteLine($"Bars: {data.Bars.Count}");

var last = data.Bars[^1];
Console.WriteLine($"{DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(last.Time).UtcDateTime}: " +
                  $"O {last.Open:F5} H {last.High:F5} L {last.Low:F5} C {last.Close:F5}");

docs.title: 2) Simple moving average over the window
docs.text:
var data = await acc.PriceHistoryAsync(new PriceHistoryRequest
{
    Symbol = "EURUSD", Timeframe = 16385,
    FromTime = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(-5).ToUnixTimeSeconds(),
    ToTime   = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
});

if (data.Bars.Count > 0)
{
    double sma = data.Bars.Average(b => b.Close);
    Console.WriteLine($"SMA(close) over {data.Bars.Count} bars = {sma:F5}");
}

docs.title: ✅ Checking if Symbol Exists
docs.text:
Request: check symbol existence from MT5. Verify if a symbol with a specified name exists (standard or custom).

API Information:

  • SDK wrapper: MT5Account.SymbolExistAsync(...) (from NuGet package MetaRPC.MT5)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolExist (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolExist(SymbolExistRequest) → SymbolExistReply
  • Low‑level client (generated): MarketInfo.SymbolExist(request, headers, deadline, cancellationToken)
  • SDK wrapper (your class):
namespace MetaRPC.CSharpMT5
{
    public class MT5Account
    {
        public async Task<SymbolExistData> SymbolExistAsync(
            string symbol,
            DateTime? deadline = null,
            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

SymbolExistRequest { name: string }

Reply message:

SymbolExistReply { data: SymbolExistData } or { error: Error }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description symbol string ✅ Symbol name to check (e.g., "EURUSD", "BTCUSD") deadline DateTime? ❌ Absolute per‑call UTC deadline → converted to timeout cancellationToken CancellationToken ❌ Cooperative cancel for the call/retry loop

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolExistData
docs.text: Field Type Description Exists bool true if symbol exists (standard or custom), false if not found IsCustom bool true if the detected symbol is a custom symbol, false for standard symbols (see MQL5 Custom Symbols)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC checking if a symbol exists and whether it's custom.
  • Why you need it. Validate symbol names before trading, check if broker supports a symbol, detect custom symbols.
  • Two flags. Exists tells if found, IsCustom tells if it's a custom (synthetic) symbol.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Verify a symbol name before attempting to trade or get quotes.
  • Check if your broker supports a specific symbol.
  • Detect whether a symbol is standard or custom/synthetic.
  • Validate user input (symbol names) in your trading application.
  • Handle different symbols gracefully (fail early if symbol doesn't exist).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Symbol names are case-sensitive in some brokers (use exact spelling: "EURUSD" not "eurusd").
  • If Exists=false, the symbol is not available from your broker.
  • If Exists=true and IsCustom=true, the symbol is synthetic/custom - may have different trading rules.
  • Use this before SymbolSelectAsync() to avoid errors when adding symbols to Market Watch.
  • Fast operation - use short timeout (3-5s).
  • Standard symbols: forex pairs, stocks, indices, commodities from broker.
  • Custom symbols: user-created synthetic instruments, spreads, custom data feeds.

docs.title: 1) Check if symbol exists
docs.text:
// Verify EURUSD is available
var result = await acc.SymbolExistAsync(
    "EURUSD",
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));

if (result.Exists)
{
    Console.WriteLine("✅ EURUSD exists");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("❌ EURUSD not found");
}

docs.title: 2) Detect custom symbols
docs.text:
// Check if symbol is custom/synthetic
var btc = await acc.SymbolExistAsync("BTCUSD");

Console.WriteLine($"Exists:   {btc.Exists}");
Console.WriteLine($"Custom:   {btc.IsCustom}");

if (btc.Exists && btc.IsCustom)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ This is a custom/synthetic symbol");
}

docs.title: 3) Validate user input
docs.text:
// Validate symbol before trading
string userSymbol = "GBPJPY"; // from user input

var check = await acc.SymbolExistAsync(userSymbol);

if (!check.Exists)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ Error: Symbol '{userSymbol}' not available");
    return;
}

Console.WriteLine($"✅ Symbol '{userSymbol}' is valid");
// Continue with trading logic...

docs.title: 4) Check multiple symbols
docs.text:
// Verify a list of symbols
var symbols = new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "XAUUSD" };

Console.WriteLine("Checking symbols:");
foreach (var sym in symbols)
{
    var result = await acc.SymbolExistAsync(sym);
    var status = result.Exists ? "✅" : "❌";
    var type = result.IsCustom ? "(custom)" : "(standard)";
    Console.WriteLine($"  {status} {sym,-10} {(result.Exists ? type : "")}");
}

docs.title: 5) Safe symbol selection
docs.text:
// Check existence before adding to Market Watch
var symbol = "EURUSD";
var exists = await acc.SymbolExistAsync(symbol);

if (!exists.Exists)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ Cannot add '{symbol}': symbol doesn't exist");
    return;
}

// Symbol exists - safe to add to Market Watch
var selected = await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(symbol, select: true);
Console.WriteLine($"✅ '{symbol}' added to Market Watch");

MQL5 Reference: SymbolInfoDouble

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning one numeric property of a symbol.
  • Why you need it. Get current prices, calculate position sizes, check trading constraints, retrieve margin requirements.
  • Most common. SymbolBid, SymbolAsk, SymbolPoint, SymbolVolumeMin/MAX/STEP, SymbolTradeContractSize.
  • 60 properties covering prices, volumes, swaps, margins, sessions, options.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Get current Bid/Ask prices (alternative to SymbolInfoTickAsync).
  • Calculate position sizes based on volume constraints.
  • Retrieve tick value for profit calculations.
  • Check swap values before holding overnight positions.
  • Get margin requirements for risk management.
  • Obtain contract size for lot-to-units conversion.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• SymbolBid/ASK - use SymbolInfoTickAsync() for faster Bid/Ask retrieval.
  • SymbolPoint - minimum price change (e.g., 0.00001 for EURUSD).
  • SymbolVolumeMin/MAX/STEP - critical for validating lot sizes before trading.
  • SymbolTradeContractSize - lot size in base currency units (e.g., 100,000 for Forex standard lot).
  • Swap values - charged for positions held overnight (positive = you earn, negative = you pay).
  • Margin requirements - used for calculating required margin before opening positions.
  • Properties are cached - use short timeout (3-5s).
  • Some properties may return 0 if not applicable (e.g., options Greeks for Forex).

docs.text:
// Get current Bid and Ask
var bid = await acc.SymbolInfoDoubleAsync(
    "EURUSD",
    SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.SymbolBid,
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));
var ask = await acc.SymbolInfoDoubleAsync(
    "EURUSD",
    SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.SymbolAsk);

Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD Bid: {bid.Value:F5}, Ask: {ask.Value:F5}");

Console.WriteLine($"  Min:  {volumeMin.Value:F2} lots");
Console.WriteLine($"  Max:  {volumeMax.Value:F2} lots");
Console.WriteLine($"  Step: {volumeStep.Value:F2} lots");

var point = await acc.SymbolInfoDoubleAsync(symbol, SymbolInfoDoubleProperty.SymbolPoint);

// Get swap values for overnight positions

    "EURUSD",

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning one integer property of a symbol.
  • Why you need it. Check digits, spread, trading restrictions, execution modes, stops level, symbol status.
  • Most common. SymbolDigits (precision), SymbolSpread (current spread), SymbolTradeStopsLevel (min SL/TP distance).
  • 37 properties covering precision, trading modes, status flags, execution parameters.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Get symbol precision (digits) for price formatting.
  • Check current spread in points.
  • Verify minimum stops level before setting SL/TP.
  • Check if symbol is selected/visible in Market Watch.
  • Determine execution mode and trading restrictions.
  • Get freeze level to avoid order modification errors.
  • Check expiration/filling modes supported by symbol.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• SymbolDigits - decimal places (5 for EURUSD = 1.12345, 2 for XAUUSD = 1925.42).
  • SymbolSpread - current spread in points (not pips!). For EURUSD with 5 digits, 10 points = 1 pip.
  • SymbolTradeStopsLevel - minimum distance from current price for SL/TP. 0 = no restriction.
  • SymbolTradeFreezeLevel - distance within which you cannot modify/close orders.
  • Boolean flags return 1 (true) or 0 (false) as long.
  • Enum properties return integer enum values - need to map to enum types.
  • Bitmask properties (EXPIRATION_MODE, FILLING_MODE, ORDER_MODE) use bitwise flags.
  • Properties are cached - use short timeout (3-5s).

docs.title: 1) Get symbol precision
docs.text:
// Get number of decimal places
var digits = await acc.SymbolInfoIntegerAsync(
    "EURUSD",
    SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SymbolDigits,
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));

Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD Digits: {digits.Value}");
// Output: 5 (prices like 1.12345)

docs.title: 2) Get current spread
docs.text:
// Get spread in points
var spread = await acc.SymbolInfoIntegerAsync(
    "GBPUSD",
    SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SymbolSpread);

var digits = await acc.SymbolInfoIntegerAsync(
    "GBPUSD",
    SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SymbolDigits);

// Convert points to pips
double pips = spread.Value / Math.Pow(10, digits.Value - 1);

Console.WriteLine($"GBPUSD Spread: {spread.Value} points ({pips:F1} pips)");

// Get minimum SL/TP distance
var stopsLevel = await acc.SymbolInfoIntegerAsync(
    "EURUSD",

{
    Console.WriteLine("✅ No stops level restriction");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ Minimum SL/TP distance: {stopsLevel.Value} points");

docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning one string property of a symbol.
  • Why you need it. Get symbol description, currencies, metadata for display, logging, or trading logic.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Display symbol's full description in UI (e.g., "Euro vs US Dollar").
  • Get base and profit currencies for position size calculations.
  • Retrieve margin currency for margin calculations.
  • Get exchange name for stocks/futures.
  • Obtain ISIN code for regulatory compliance.
  • Display symbol metadata in logs or reports.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• SymbolCurrencyBase - the first currency in a pair (for EURUSD = EUR).
  • SymbolCurrencyProfit - currency of profit/loss (for EURUSD = USD).
  • SymbolCurrencyMargin - currency used for margin (usually same as profit).
  • For Forex pairs: Base/Profit (e.g., EUR/USD means EUR is base, USD is profit).
  • Some properties may return empty strings if not available from broker.
  • Use short timeout (3-5s) as this is metadata (cached).
  • SymbolFormula is for custom symbols only - synthetic instruments.
  • SymbolIsin availability depends on broker/instrument type.

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning the latest tick (price quote) for a symbol.
  • Why you need it. Get current market prices, calculate spreads, check last update time, verify quotes before trading.
  • Key fields. Bid (sell price), Ask (buy price), Time (when updated).
  • Performance. Fast snapshot of current market state.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Get current Bid/Ask prices before placing an order.
  • Calculate the current spread (Ask - Bid).
  • Check when the last price update occurred.
  • Verify symbol has active quotes.
  • Monitor price changes in real-time (polling).
  • Get Last price and volume for exchange-traded instruments.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Bid = price at which you can sell (broker buys from you).
  • Ask = price at which you can buy (broker sells to you).
  • Spread = Ask - Bid (broker's markup, in price units).
  • Time is Unix timestamp in seconds - use DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(tick.Time) to convert.
  • TimeMsc provides millisecond precision for high-frequency trading.
  • Last and Volume are primarily used for exchange-traded instruments (stocks, futures).
  • For Forex, Bid and Ask are the main prices - Last may be 0.
  • Ensure symbol is in Market Watch and synchronized before calling.
  • Use short timeout (3-5s) as quotes update frequently.
  • For real-time monitoring, consider using streaming API (SubscribeToTicksAsync) instead of polling.

docs.title: 1) Get current Bid/Ask
docs.text:
// Get current prices for EURUSD
var tick = await acc.SymbolInfoTickAsync(
    "EURUSD",
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));

Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD:");
Console.WriteLine($"  Bid: {tick.Bid:F5}");
Console.WriteLine($"  Ask: {tick.Ask:F5}");

docs.title: 2) Calculate spread
docs.text:
// Calculate current spread
var tick = await acc.SymbolInfoTickAsync("EURUSD");

double spread = tick.Ask - tick.Bid;
Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD Spread: {spread:F5} ({spread * 10000:F1} pips)");

docs.title: 3) Check quote freshness
docs.text:
// Verify quote is recent
var tick = await acc.SymbolInfoTickAsync("GBPUSD");

var quoteTime = DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(tick.Time).DateTime;
var age = DateTime.UtcNow - quoteTime;

Console.WriteLine($"Quote time: {quoteTime:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss} UTC");
Console.WriteLine($"Quote age:  {age.TotalSeconds:F1} seconds");

if (age.TotalSeconds > 10)
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ Quote is stale (older than 10 seconds)");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("✅ Quote is fresh");
}

docs.title: 4) Display multiple symbols
docs.text:
// Show current prices for multiple symbols
var symbols = new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "XAUUSD" };

Console.WriteLine("Current Market Prices:");
Console.WriteLine("Symbol      Bid         Ask         Spread");
Console.WriteLine("──────────────────────────────────────────────");

foreach (var sym in symbols)
{
    var tick = await acc.SymbolInfoTickAsync(sym);
    double spread = tick.Ask - tick.Bid;
    Console.WriteLine($"{sym,-10}  {tick.Bid,-10:F5}  {tick.Ask,-10:F5}  {spread:F5}");
}

// High-precision price monitoring
var tick = await acc.SymbolInfoTickAsync("EURUSD");

var timeMsc = DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeMilliseconds(tick.TimeMsc).DateTime;

Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD Tick:");
Console.WriteLine($"  Time (ms):   {timeMsc:yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff} UTC");
Console.WriteLine($"  Bid:         {tick.Bid:F5}");
Console.WriteLine($"  Ask:         {tick.Ask:F5}");
Console.WriteLine($"  Last:        {tick.Last:F5}");
Console.WriteLine($"  Volume:      {tick.Volume}");
Console.WriteLine($"  Volume Real: {tick.VolumeReal:F2}");

docs.text: Field Type Description Synchronized bool true if data are synchronized with server, false if not synchronized or stale

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC checking if symbol's market data is synchronized with the trade server.
  • Why you need it. Ensure quotes are fresh before trading, detect connection issues, wait for data after adding symbol.
  • Use case. After SymbolSelectAsync(), check if data is synchronized before requesting quotes or placing orders.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Verify symbol data is up-to-date before trading operations.
  • Wait for synchronization after adding a symbol to Market Watch.
  • Detect connection/data feed issues for specific symbols.
  • Ensure quotes are fresh before calculating trading parameters.
  • Diagnose why quotes might be missing or stale.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Check after SymbolSelectAsync() - newly added symbols may take time to sync.
  • If Synchronized=false, symbol data might be stale or connection is poor.
  • Use retry logic with delays when waiting for synchronization (e.g., after adding symbol).
  • Fast operation - use short timeout (3-5s).
  • Symbols not in Market Watch may always return false.
  • During market close, some symbols may not be synchronized (normal behavior).
  • Don't trade if not synchronized - quotes may be outdated.

docs.title: 1) Check if symbol is synchronized
docs.text:
// Check EURUSD synchronization status
var result = await acc.SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync(
    symbol: "EURUSD",
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));

if (result.Synchronized)
{
    Console.WriteLine("✅ EURUSD data is synchronized");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ EURUSD data is NOT synchronized");
}

docs.title: 2) Wait for synchronization after adding symbol
docs.text:
// Add symbol and wait for synchronization
var symbol = "GBPJPY";

// Add to Market Watch
await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(symbol, select: true);
Console.WriteLine($"Added {symbol} to Market Watch");

// Wait for synchronization (with retries)
bool isSynced = false;
for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 10; attempt++)
{
    var result = await acc.SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync(symbol);
    if (result.Synchronized)
    {
        isSynced = true;
        break;
    }

    Console.WriteLine($"  Waiting for sync... (attempt {attempt + 1})");
    await Task.Delay(500); // Wait 500ms before retry
}

if (isSynced)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"✅ {symbol} synchronized and ready");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ {symbol} failed to synchronize");
}

docs.title: 3) Verify before trading
docs.text:
// Ensure symbol is synchronized before placing order
var symbol = "EURUSD";

// Check synchronization
var syncStatus = await acc.SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync(symbol);

if (!syncStatus.Synchronized)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ Cannot trade {symbol}: data not synchronized");
    return;
}

// Safe to get quotes and trade
var tick = await acc.SymbolInfoTickAsync(symbol);
Console.WriteLine($"✅ {symbol} Bid: {tick.Bid}, Ask: {tick.Ask}");
// Continue with trading...

docs.title: 4) Check multiple symbols
docs.text:
// Verify synchronization for multiple symbols
var symbols = new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "XAUUSD" };

Console.WriteLine("Symbol synchronization status:");
foreach (var sym in symbols)
{
    var result = await acc.SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync(sym);
    var status = result.Synchronized ? "✅" : "⚠️";
    var text = result.Synchronized ? "synced" : "NOT synced";
    Console.WriteLine($"  {status} {sym,-10} {text}");
}

docs.title: 5) Diagnostic check for connection issues
docs.text:
// Check if any selected symbols are not synchronized (connection issue)
var total = await acc.SymbolsTotalAsync(selectedOnly: true);
int notSyncedCount = 0;

for (int i = 0; i < total.Total; i++)
{
    var symbolData = await acc.SymbolNameAsync(i, selected: true);
    var syncStatus = await acc.SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync(symbolData.Name);

    if (!syncStatus.Synchronized)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ {symbolData.Name} not synchronized");
        notSyncedCount++;
    }
}

if (notSyncedCount == 0)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"✅ All {total.Total} symbols synchronized");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"⚠️ {notSyncedCount} of {total.Total} symbols not synchronized");
}

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC returning symbol name by its index in the list.
  • Why you need it. Iterate through symbols, enumerate Market Watch, discover available symbols.
  • Two modes. selected=true → symbols in Market Watch, selected=false → all available symbols.
  • Index-based. Use with SymbolsTotalAsync() to get the count first, then iterate by index.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Enumerate all symbols in Market Watch (iterate from 0 to SymbolsTotal-1).
  • Discover all available symbols from your broker.
  • Build a list of trading instruments for your application.
  • Get the first/last symbol in the list.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Always call SymbolsTotalAsync() first to get the valid index range.
  • Index is zero-based: first symbol = 0, last symbol = total - 1.
  • If index is out of range, you'll get an error.
  • Use selected=true for symbols currently in Market Watch (faster, smaller list).
  • Use selected=false to discover all symbols your broker offers.
  • The order of symbols may change if Market Watch is modified during iteration.
  • Fast operation - use short timeout (3-5s).

docs.title: 1) Get first symbol from Market Watch
docs.text:
// Get the first symbol in Market Watch
var firstSymbol = await acc.SymbolNameAsync(
    index: 0,
    selected: true,
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));
Console.WriteLine($"First symbol: {firstSymbol.Name}");

docs.title: 2) Enumerate all symbols in Market Watch
docs.text:
// Get count and iterate through all Market Watch symbols
var total = await acc.SymbolsTotalAsync(selectedOnly: true);

Console.WriteLine($"Symbols in Market Watch ({total.Total}):");
for (int i = 0; i < total.Total; i++)
{
    var symbolData = await acc.SymbolNameAsync(index: i, selected: true);
    Console.WriteLine($"  [{i}] {symbolData.Name}");
}

docs.title: 3) Get all available symbols from broker
docs.text:
// Enumerate all symbols broker offers (not just Market Watch)
var totalAll = await acc.SymbolsTotalAsync(selectedOnly: false);

Console.WriteLine($"All available symbols ({totalAll.Total}):");
for (int i = 0; i < Math.Min(totalAll.Total, 10); i++) // Show first 10
{
    var symbolData = await acc.SymbolNameAsync(index: i, selected: false);
    Console.WriteLine($"  [{i}] {symbolData.Name}");
}
Console.WriteLine($"... and {totalAll.Total - 10} more");

docs.title: 4) Build symbol list
docs.text:
// Create a list of all symbols in Market Watch
var total = await acc.SymbolsTotalAsync(selectedOnly: true);
var symbolList = new List<string>();

for (int i = 0; i < total.Total; i++)
{
    var symbolData = await acc.SymbolNameAsync(i, selected: true);
    symbolList.Add(symbolData.Name);
}

Console.WriteLine($"Loaded {symbolList.Count} symbols:");
Console.WriteLine(string.Join(", ", symbolList));

docs.title: 5) Find specific symbol by iteration
docs.text:
// Search for a symbol by iterating (not efficient, but demonstrates usage)
var total = await acc.SymbolsTotalAsync(selectedOnly: true);
string targetSymbol = "EURUSD";
int foundIndex = -1;

for (int i = 0; i < total.Total; i++)
{
    var symbolData = await acc.SymbolNameAsync(i, selected: true);
    if (symbolData.Name == targetSymbol)
    {
        foundIndex = i;
        break;
    }
}

if (foundIndex >= 0)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"✅ Found '{targetSymbol}' at index {foundIndex}");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ '{targetSymbol}' not in Market Watch");
}

namespace MetaRPC.CSharpMT5

            string symbol,

            CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
    }
}

Request message:

SymbolSelectRequest { symbol: string, select: bool }

Reply message:

SymbolSelectReply { data: SymbolSelectData } or { error: Error }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description symbol string ✅ Symbol name (e.g., "EURUSD") select bool ✅ true - add symbol to Market Watch, false - remove symbol from Market Watch deadline DateTime? ❌ Absolute per‑call UTC deadline → converted to timeout cancellationToken CancellationToken ❌ Cooperative cancel for the call/retry loop

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolSelectData
docs.text: Field Type Description Success bool true if operation succeeded, false if failed

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Single RPC to add/remove symbols from Market Watch.
  • Why you need it. Enable symbols for trading, receive quotes, ensure symbol data is available.
  • Two modes. select=true → add to Market Watch, select=false → remove from Market Watch.
  • Important. Symbol cannot be removed if chart is open or there are open positions.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use this method when you need to:

  • Add symbols to Market Watch before trading or getting quotes.
  • Ensure a symbol is visible and receiving data updates.
  • Clean up Market Watch by removing unused symbols.
  • Prepare symbols for trading operations.
  • Dynamically manage Market Watch list based on trading strategy.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Always add symbols to Market Watch before trading - many operations require the symbol to be selected.
  • If Success=false, check: symbol might not exist, chart might be open, or positions might be active.
  • Cannot remove symbol if:
  • A chart for this symbol is open in MT5 terminal
  • There are open positions for this symbol
  • Symbol is being used by an active order
  • Use SymbolExistAsync() first to verify symbol exists before selecting.
  • Selecting an already-selected symbol returns Success=true (idempotent operation).
  • Fast operation - use short timeout (3-5s).
  • Some brokers automatically select symbols when you open positions - check with SymbolsTotalAsync().

docs.title: 1) Add symbol to Market Watch
docs.text:
// Add EURUSD to Market Watch
var result = await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(
    symbol: "EURUSD",
    select: true,
    deadline: DateTime.UtcNow.AddSeconds(3));

if (result.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine("✅ EURUSD added to Market Watch");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("❌ Failed to add EURUSD");
}

docs.title: 2) Remove symbol from Market Watch
docs.text:
// Remove GBPJPY from Market Watch
var result = await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(
    symbol: "GBPJPY",
    select: false);

if (result.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine("✅ GBPJPY removed from Market Watch");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("⚠️ Cannot remove GBPJPY (chart open or positions active?)");
}

docs.title: 3) Ensure symbol is available before trading
docs.text:
// Ensure symbol is in Market Watch before placing order
var symbol = "EURUSD";

// Check if exists
var exists = await acc.SymbolExistAsync(symbol);
if (!exists.Exists)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ Symbol '{symbol}' doesn't exist");
    return;
}

// Add to Market Watch
var selected = await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(symbol, select: true);
if (!selected.Success)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ Failed to add '{symbol}' to Market Watch");
    return;
}

Console.WriteLine($"✅ '{symbol}' ready for trading");
// Continue with trading operations...

docs.title: 4) Add multiple symbols
docs.text:
// Add a list of symbols to Market Watch
var symbols = new[] { "EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "XAUUSD" };

Console.WriteLine("Adding symbols to Market Watch:");
foreach (var sym in symbols)
{
    var result = await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(sym, select: true);
    var status = result.Success ? "✅" : "❌";
    Console.WriteLine($"  {status} {sym}");
}

docs.title: 5) Toggle symbol visibility
docs.text:
// Toggle symbol in Market Watch
var symbol = "BTCUSD";
bool shouldAdd = true; // from user input or logic

var result = await acc.SymbolSelectAsync(symbol, select: shouldAdd);

if (result.Success)
{
    var action = shouldAdd ? "added to" : "removed from";
    Console.WriteLine($"✅ {symbol} {action} Market Watch");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine($"❌ Failed to modify {symbol}");
}

docs.title: MT5Account · Symbol Information - Overview
docs.text: Symbol properties, trading sessions, market data, and symbol availability. Use this page to choose the right API for accessing symbol information.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• SymbolInfoDouble - single double value from symbol (bid, ask, spread, tick size, etc.).
  • SymbolInfoInteger - single integer value from symbol (digits, spread, time flags, etc.).
  • SymbolInfoString - single string value from symbol (description, path, category, etc.).
  • SymbolInfoTick - latest tick data for symbol (bid, ask, last, volume, time).
  • SymbolsTotal - count of available symbols (all or Market Watch only).
  • SymbolExist - check if symbol exists (standard or custom).
  • SymbolName - get symbol name by index from list.
  • SymbolSelect - add/remove symbol to/from Market Watch.
  • SymbolIsSynchronized - check if symbol data is synchronized with server.
  • SymbolList - full list of all available symbol names in one call.
  • PriceHistory - historical OHLC bars for a symbol and timeframe over a time window.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• SymbolInfo* (Double/Integer/String) → grab one specific property of a symbol.
  • SymbolInfoTick → get current market prices (bid/ask) for a symbol.
  • SymbolsTotal → count how many symbols are available.
  • SymbolExist → verify if a symbol exists before trading.
  • SymbolSelect → enable symbol for quotes and trading.
  • SymbolName → iterate through symbols by index.
  • SymbolIsSynchronized → ensure data is fresh before trading.

Rule of thumb: need one property → SymbolInfo*Async; need current prices → SymbolInfoTickAsync; need symbol management → Select/Exist/IsSynchronized.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Key inputs One numeric value (bid, ask, spread, etc.) SymbolInfoDoubleAsync Single double Symbol name + Property enum One integer value (digits, time flags, etc.) SymbolInfoIntegerAsync Single long Symbol name + Property enum One text value (description, currency, etc.) SymbolInfoStringAsync Single string Symbol name + Property enum Current market prices (bid/ask/last) SymbolInfoTickAsync MrpcMqlTick object Symbol name Count of available symbols SymbolsTotalAsync int Selected only (true/false) Check if symbol exists SymbolExistAsync Exists + IsCustom flags Symbol name Get symbol name by index SymbolNameAsync string Index + Selected flag Add/remove symbol from Market Watch SymbolSelectAsync Success flag Symbol name + Select flag Check if symbol data is synchronized SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync bool Symbol name

docs.title: ❌ Cross‑refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• SymbolSelect must be called before accessing quotes for some symbols.
  • Spread is in points, not pips - divide by 10 for 5-digit brokers.
  • Tick size determines minimum price change - important for pending orders.
  • Contract size affects lot calculations - 1 lot = contract size units.
  • Digits determines price precision - use for rounding prices.
  • Session times vary by broker and symbol - check trading hours.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
// Get current bid/ask prices
var tick = await account.SymbolInfoTickAsync("EURUSD");
Console.WriteLine($"EURUSD - Bid: {tick.Bid:F5}, Ask: {tick.Ask:F5}, Spread: {(tick.Ask - tick.Bid) * 100000:F1} points");

// Get symbol spread
var spread = await account.SymbolInfoIntegerAsync("EURUSD",
    SymbolInfoIntegerProperty.SymbolSpread);
Console.WriteLine($"Spread: {spread} points");

// Check if symbol exists before trading
var existData = await account.SymbolExistAsync("BTCUSD");
if (existData.Exists)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Symbol exists! Is custom: {existData.IsCustom}");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("Symbol not found!");
}

// Add symbol to Market Watch
var success = await account.SymbolSelectAsync("XAUUSD", select: true);
if (success.Success)
{
    // Wait for synchronization
    var synced = await account.SymbolIsSynchronizedAsync("XAUUSD");
    if (synced.Synchronized)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Symbol ready for trading!");
    }
}

// Iterate through all symbols in Market Watch
var total = await account.SymbolsTotalAsync(selectedOnly: true);
for (int i = 0; i < total.Total; i++)
{
    var symbolData = await account.SymbolNameAsync(i, selected: true);
    Console.WriteLine($"[{i}] {symbolData.Name}");
}

  • Trading: OrderSend - place orders using symbol names

  • Additional: SymbolParamsMany - get detailed symbol properties
